Title: Thousands evacuate after Indonesia quake kills 51, cuts roads
Article:
SIKKA: Around 5,000 people have been evacuated after a magnitude-7.7 earthquake smashed an area in eastern Indonesia, killing at least 51, blocking roads and causing landslides, authorities said on Sunday.
Thirty-six people were seriously injured in the Saturday morning quake in East Nusa Tenggara province, while 77 had minor injuries, Deputy Health Minister Benjamin Paulus Octavianus told a televised meeting.
The quake, followed by some 341 aftershocks, is the Southeast Asian nation's worst in years. Hundreds died after a 2022 earthquake in West Java.
More than 3,300 people in the Sikka region self-evacuated or were stranded in a sports arena, said the disaster mitigation agency BNPB.
Some Sikka residents were stranded outside collapsed homes under a makeshift tent made out of tarp, while some people received treatment in a tent outside a hospital in the port town of Maumere.
"Almost all of Sikka's residents didn't dare stay indoors, so they slept on a porch or a tent outside," Simon Sabandi, deputy regent of Sikka, told news channel KompasTV.
More than 3,500 military and police officers have been deployed to the region, Cabinet Secretary Teddy Indra Wijaya said in a statement.
Rescuers were able to access parts of Maumere that had been blocked by landslides, Indonesia's search and rescue agency said. Most of those missing were trapped under rubble, and more than 1,300 homes were damaged, BNPB said.
Twenty petrol stations were not operational due to power outages, said state energy firm Pertamina.
The East Nusa Tenggara government is considering declaring an emergency for the province, BNPB said, which would allow authorities to mobilise resources and funding.
The area of the quake was hit in 1992 by a magnitude-7.5 earthquake that caused extensive destruction, Indonesia's geophysics agency said.
Indonesia, a sprawling archipelago of 290 million people, straddles the "Pacific Ring of Fire", a seismically active zone where tectonic plates meet, triggering frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.

Title: DAP backs Anwar's plan to abolish AUKU, urges wider reforms
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: DAP will give its full support to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's proposal to abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU), while urging the government to apply the same momentum to other longstanding promises.
Secretary-general Anthony Loke said the abolition of AUKU had been a cause championed by DAP for decades, describing the prime minister's announcement as a significant moment.
"DAP will give him 100 per cent support. But we appeal — not just AUKU.
"That same spirit must be carried forward for several more reforms that we have promised to the people," he said in his policy address at the DAP national congress here today.
He said the more fundamental issue in education was ensuring equal access to public universities, and that no Malaysian should be denied the opportunity to pursue higher education based on race.
"Every Malaysian who achieves acceptable results should be entitled to a place in a public university.
"This should be the policy and the spirit of reform that the prime minister seeks to bring," he said.
Loke, who said he had been educated at a local university and had personally experienced what he described as a climate of fear on campus under AUKU, said the Act's abolition should be seen as a beginning rather than an end point for educational reform.
Loke said DAP would support any proposal, formula or policy from the prime minister and the Cabinet that reduced the cost of doing business, increased household incomes and eased the cost of living, but stressed that announcements alone were insufficient.
"We will give our support, but what is most important is decisive implementation and firm decisions by the prime minister and the Cabinet," he said.
He added that whatever decision delegates made at the congress regarding the party's future in government, DAP's primary objective remained achieving meaningful, positive change to make Malaysia a progressive country.
Yesterday, Anwar announced in his policy speech as PKR president that the government would
abolish
AUKU.
He said that although several amendments had previously been made, some matters remained unsatisfactory to university students.
Anwar said the proposal will be tabled at the Cabinet meeting this Wednesday.

Title: Eastern Japan rain kills nine: Report
Article:
TOKYO: Heavy rain that battered eastern Japan has left nine people dead, public broadcaster NHK said Sunday, after an "unprecedented" deluge that flooded over a thousand homes and snarled up roads and rail services.
Torrential downpours starting late Thursday triggered landslide warnings and power outages, with forecasters issuing the highest-level heavy rain warning for the Chiba region for the first time.
A weather station in the prefecture recorded 30 centimetres of rain in 24 hours, making it the area's wettest August in six decades.
By Friday morning, the city of Chiba logged more than three times the rainfall typically seen in the whole of August, Tokyo's land ministry said.
Nine have since died in the rains, NHK reported Sunday morning, citing its own tally.
Chiba's disaster management office as of Saturday evening listed eight dead, some trapped inside submerged cars and others found on flooded streets.
Over 70 houses across the Chiba region were partially destroyed by the rain, the prefecture's latest tally showed.
And over a thousand households reported being flooded, nearly 600 of which saw water surge above the floorboards.
An estimated 1,200 cars also remain abandoned on roads, local media said, with authorities working on towing them away or using jacks to move them.
An official from Japan's Meteorological Agency told a news conference on Thursday that it was "shaping up to be an unprecedented level of heavy rain."
Scientists say human-driven climate change is making extreme weather more frequent, prolonged and intense.

Title: Ramanan calls for unity among PKR leaders
Article:
AYER KEROH: PKR leaders must stop attacking one another as internal disputes risk splitting the party at the grassroots and weakening its machinery, vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan warned today.
Ramanan said conflicts among leaders at the top would eventually have repercussions on branches and members on the ground.
"If we keep attacking one another at the top, those who will ultimately suffer are our machinery on the ground.
"Divisions will split. Branches will split. Members will become confused. The machinery will weaken. And in the end, it is our political opponents who will benefit," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress here.
Ramanan said party leaders and members must remember that no individual or personal interest was greater than PKR and its wider struggle.
He called on those with differences to resolve them through discussion rather than allowing disagreements or personal egos to divide the party.
"Remember, no one is bigger than the party. No personal interest is greater than the struggle.
"If there are differences, we sit down at the same table. If there are problems, we resolve them as one family. If there are egos, we put them aside," he said.
Ramanan added that maintaining unity was crucial as the party's broader objectives were more important than the interests of any single individual.
"Our goal is far greater than any one individual," he said.

Title: GOF personnel injured as suspected migrant smuggler reverses car into him
Article:
TUMPAT: A General Operations Force (GOF) personnel was injured after a car driven by a suspected migrant smuggler hit him while attempting to flee during an operation in Kampung Chat, Palekbang, last night.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the 29-year-old corporal sustained injuries to his head, hands, body and knees in the 8.30pm incident.
He said the personnel was admitted to Tumpat Hospital, where he received two stitches to the back of his head.
"Acting on public tip-offs, the GOF personnel and his team from the Seventh Battalion stopped a Proton Preve when it passed Jalan Kampung Chat.
"Seeing the officers, the driver acted aggressively and attempted to escape by reversing the vehicle
"One of the personnel was injured in the incident while another escaped unhurt. The driver was detained," he said.
Ahmad Radzi said the 34-year-old driver, from Kampung Kenat Bunut Susu, had 15 previous criminal offences, including drug-related offences, vehicle theft and offences under the Penal Code and Immigration Act.
Six Myanmar women, aged between 21 and 31, who were in the vehicle and failed to produce valid identification documents were also detained.
"Earlier investigations found that the six women had entered Malaysia through an illegal route in Pulau Besar.
"They allegedly dealt with a Myanmar agent through Facebook Messenger and paid RM6,000 each," he said.
The GOF also seized four suspected yaba pills hidden in a cigarette box in the driver's door compartment, eight mobile phones and the Proton Preve, with the total estimated value of the seizures at RM42,000.
"The driver tested positive for amphetamine during an initial urine screening," he added.
Ahmad Radzi said the suspect also admitted to receiving RM70 for transporting each undocumented migrant to Kota Baru, with payment allegedly made in cash by a Malaysian man after the migrants were delivered.
The case is being investigated under several provisions of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act, Immigration Act, Penal Code and Dangerous Drugs Act.
All suspects and seized items were handed over to the Tumpat district police station for further investigation.

Title: Kelantan health authorities monitor newborn exposed to drugs in womb
Article:
KOTA BARU: The Kelantan Health Department is monitoring a newborn girl who tested positive for amphetamines and benzodiazepines following a urine screening at the Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital (HRPZ II) Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) on Aug 6.
Deputy health director Dr Rohana Daud said the mother was believed to have taken sedatives, prompting health officials to monitor the infant for withdrawal symptoms.
She said the baby was still receiving treatment in hospital as of last week, with her Finnegan Score — used to assess neonatal withdrawal symptoms — dropping to zero while under medical care.
"Such symptoms are usually temporary and full recovery is expected. However, health authorities will continue follow-up treatment to ensure the child's development is not affected," she said.
Rohana said this after officiating the USM House Officer Preparatory Course 2026 at the Universiti Sains Malaysia Specialist Hospital auditorium in Kubang Kerian today.
On the effects of maternal drug use, she said substances could pass from the mother to the fetus through the umbilical cord.
She said similar cases had occurred previously but remained isolated, adding that multi-agency intervention, including the Social Welfare Department and hospital social workers, would be initiated under the Child Act to protect the infant.
It was previously reported that the infant
tested positive
for amphetamines and benzodiazepines during a urine screening at the NICU.
Police investigations found that the baby had been exposed to the substances in the womb, while a subsequent urine test confirmed the mother was positive for benzodiazepines following her arrest.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke apologises to DAP delegates over Chennah defeat
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has apologised to party delegates over the loss of the Chennah state seat in the Negri Sembilan election.
Addressing the party's National Congress at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre today, Loke said the defeat left him with "a deep sense of sadness."
This was his
first electoral loss
in 22 years.
"I apologise to the delegates for this defeat in Chennah," he said.
Loke said he contested the Malay-majority constituency to demonstrate that DAP could win support across communities.
"However, I must admit that this mission did not succeed," he said.
He noted that DAP secured between 20 and 25 per cent of Malay voter support and strong backing from the Orang Asli community.
"This is a major challenge for DAP: how do we break through this barrier so that our political journey can carry us further?" Loke said, adding that the party must find ways to dismantle the "wall of racial politics."
Loke lost the Chennah seat to Barisan Nasional's Siow Kong Choon by a majority of
688 votes
, ending his 13-year hold on the constituency.
Following the result, he
stepped down
as Negri Sembilan DAP chairman but remains the party's secretary-general.
"Nevertheless, the defeat in Chennah and the series of electoral setbacks in recent times should not become an obstacle to us moving forward.
"As long as we do not give up, the future of DAP will be embraced by the majority of Malaysians," he said.
He urged delegates and party activists to continue the party's multiracial mission.
"We must not give up on our dream of becoming a multiracial party accepted by all Malaysians," he said.

Title: New plans to underpin Maxis' mobile growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Maxis Bhd is expected to maintain decent consumer mobile service revenue growth, supported by new postpaid and prepaid plans launched in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026), CIMB Securities said.
Its analyst Choong Chen Foong said Maxis' consumer mobile service revenue grew 0.8 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) to RM1.58 billion in the second quarter (Q2) of 2026.
Its postpaid subscriptions rose 0.7 per cent and average revenue per user (ARPU) increased 0.3 per cent.
Maxis' prepaid subscriptions grew 0.4 per cent QoQ, while ARPU rose 1.4 per cent.
On a yearly basis, the company's consumer mobile service revenue increased 2.7 per cent, supported by the new plans launched in 1H 2026.
Its postpaid revenue grew 4.2 per cent, while prepaid revenue increased 0.3 per cent, marking its second consecutive quarter of growth.
Choong said prepaid growth was driven by a 0.8 per cent YoY increase in ARPU, reflecting better monetisation and higher-quality subscribers.
Consumer home revenue rose marginally by 0.4 per cent QoQ to RM252 million, although it declined 0.8 per cent YoY.
Home connections increased 0.7 per cent QoQ and 3.2 per cent YoY, while ARPU rose 0.6 per cent QoQ.
Enterprise service revenue eased 0.7 per cent QoQ to RM416 million but grew 2.2 per cent YoY, led by a 3.5 per cent increase in fixed and solutions revenue, supported by managed services, cloud connectivity and digital solutions.
Choong said Maxis' service earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (ebitda) margin reached a five-year high of 50.6 per cent in 2Q26, rising 0.9 percentage point QoQ, helped by lower network, staff and seasonal device costs.
Ebitda rose 2.2 per cent QoQ and 2.7 per cent YoY.
Maxis maintained its financial year 2026 (FY26) guidance for low single-digit service revenue and Ebitda growth, with a capex-to-sales ratio of 10 to 12 per cent.
CIMB Securities maintained its "Buy" call and RM4.35 target price, with FY26-FY28 core earnings forecasts unchanged.
Choong expects core net profit to grow four per cent YoY in FY26, before easing three per cent in FY27 due mainly to the full-year impact of equity accounting for Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB).
For FY28, core net profit is forecast to rebound six per cent YoY, supported by lower depreciation and a reduced share of DNB's net loss.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke tables motion at DAP national congress to decide whether party stays in Cabinet
Article:
ss
PUTRAJAYA: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has tabled a motion at the party's national congress here for delegates to decide via secret ballot whether to remain in the Cabinet.
The motion, to be decided by more than 4,000 delegates, was seconded by deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming.
Loke, who is also Transport Minister, said the central executive committee (CEC) deliberately refrained from making the call itself — a move aimed at democratising the party's decision-making process.
He reminded delegates that DAP had been in the federal government for nearly three years and eight months — longer than its first stint in power in 2018.
"We are in the federal government for the second time — after the first occasion in 2018, when after more than 50 years of struggle we finally attained power in Putrajaya.
"The first time lasted only 22 months. This second time we have been in government longer than the first. That in itself is already an achievement of which we can be proud," he said in his address.
Loke added that the choice of venue was itself symbolic, highlighting that the party's presence in the federal administrative capital reflected how far DAP had come.
"This is the first time a DAP conference has been held in Putrajaya at PICC. And today we want delegates to decide — do we remain in Putrajaya or not?" he told delegates.
Loke recounted how, in the early 1970s, after Lim Kit Siang's release from Internal Security Act detention, the late MCA president Tun Tan Siew Sin had invited the then-DAP secretary-general to dissolve the party and merge with MCA to strengthen Chinese political representation within the ruling Alliance government.
"Lim Kit Siang firmly rejected that proposal because he said DAP is not only for the Chinese — DAP has leaders and members from the Indian community, the Malay community, and it is for all Malaysians," Loke said.
He drew a direct line from that moment more than half a century ago to the congress today, reaffirming that the party's multiracial character was non-negotiable.
Loke said the motion before delegates reflected the costs of being in government — that the party had to collectively bear responsibility for unpopular decisions, absorb criticism and absorb protest votes.
"Our objective is not merely to occupy seats in government, to become ministers, deputy ministers, or key officeholders.
"What is more important is whether our struggle and our role can help contribute to a better nation," he added.
DAP has seen a decline in support since the Sabah election, where the party lost all six seats it contested.
Last month, the party won only six of the 17 seats it contested in the Johor election.
The party suffered another major setback in the Negri Sembilan election after losing two seats, including Chennah, which had been held by Loke since 2013.
In the Aug 1 state election, Loke failed to retain the seat after losing a straight fight to BN's Siow Kong Choon, the Negri Sembilan MCA Youth chief.

Title: Doctor loses RM588,000 in Dungun Forex investment scam
Article:
DUNGUN: A private doctor lost RM588,000 after she was allegedly duped by a Forex and Ethereum investment scheme promising lucrative returns, police said.
Dungun district police chief Superintendent Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said the victim was a 32-year-old who had seen an advertisement for trading or investment lessons on Instagram in January 2026.
"The victim contacted an individual via WhatsApp who introduced himself as 'Wan'.
"The victim was then asked to make a payment of RM300 to obtain videos on trading methods," he said according to Harian Metro.
He said that during the investment process, the victim was told that she had committed an offence and was required to pay compensation to avoid being charged in court.
"The frightened victim made 77 transactions to six different bank accounts.
"The victim was still asked to make further payments, causing her to realise that she had been duped," he said.
"Police have taken the victim's initial statement, received copies of the transaction receipts and applied to the banks for information on the owners of the accounts involved," he said.
He said no arrests had been made and investigations were continuing under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
Police advised the public not to be deceived by investment offers promising lucrative returns within a short period.
They should first check the legitimacy of investment offers and avoid transferring money to unknown accounts, he said.

Title: Sime Darby Property tops out first Elmina high-rise
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sime Darby Property Bhd has topped out Kanopi Residences, its first high-rise residential development in the 141.64-hectare Elmina City Centre in Sungai Buloh, Selangor.
This marks a key construction milestone ahead of the project's targeted completion in the third quarter of 2027.
The 36-storey project has a gross development value of RM299 million and comprises 499 units ranging from 550 to 1,200 square feet.
Located on Persiaran Garcinia near Elmina Lakeside Mall, Kanopi Residences is part of the 2630-hectare City of Elmina masterplan and targets young professionals, first-time homebuyers and starter families.
SD Property chief operating officer of township development Appollo Leong said the topping-out milestone reflected the company's commitment to delivering quality developments on schedule.
"As Elmina City Centre continues to grow, Kanopi Residences reflects our vision of creating a 15-minute city, with an integrated urban environment where everyday living amenities such as commercial conveniences, schools, parks and accessibility networks are within a 15-minute walk or cycle," he said in a statement.
[[nid:1512190]]
Inspired by the neighbouring Bukit Cherakah Forest Reserve, Kanopi Residences adopts an afforestation-themed concept, featuring more than 35 wellness and lifestyle facilities.
These include Co-Working in the Sky, Lounge in the Sky and Fitness in the Sky, alongside recreational and community facilities on Level 7.
The development connects to the Guthrie Corridor Expressway and Damansara-Shah Alam Elevated Expressway, while Elmina Lakeside Mall is about 300 metres away.
Residents will also have access to the 121-hectare Elmina Central Park, which features urban, community, arts and cultural, wildlife, forest and sports parks linked by a five-kilometre biodiversity corridor.
[[nid:1512189]]
Kanopi Residences is also located near several national and international schools.
Since its launch in the fourth quarter of 2024, the project has achieved a 90 per cent take-up rate, indicating a strong market response.
It also received a Gold Award in the Best Lifestyle High-Rise Development category at the PropertyGuru Asia Property Awards Malaysia 2025.
SD Property said Kanopi Residences will further expand the residential offering at Elmina City Centre and support its development of sustainable and thriving communities.

Title: PKR must focus on bread-and-butter issues, not just economic figures — Fahmi
Article:
AYER KEROH: PKR must focus more on the economic pressures faced by ordinary Malaysians, as strong macroeconomic indicators alone may not be enough to win over voters, party information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
Fahmi said indicators such as gross domestic product growth, unemployment, government revenue, trade and investment inflows reflected the broader strength of the economy, but did not necessarily translate into improvements felt by households.
He said the indicators are the broader macroeconomic picture, while issues such as wages, the cost of living and fuel prices represented the concerns that had a more immediate impact on the public.
"Many of the figures that we present — GDP growth, unemployment, international trade, government revenue and investment — I simplify these as the 'ekonomi periuk'.
"These are the basic ingredients, but they are macroeconomic matters that may not reach the people," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress here.
Fahmi said recent political developments showed that strong economic performance alone was not enough if voters continued to feel pressure in their daily lives.
"What is closest to the people, before reaching their hearts, is their stomach. From the stomach, it reaches the heart.
"Today, when people are struggling to make ends meet, all the good ingredients and spices arising from the government's achievements do not reach their stomachs and do not reach their hearts.
"So, we must address these bread-and-butter concerns and resolve issues that affect the people emotionally," he said.
Fahmi said delegates had repeatedly raised concerns over wages, the cost of living, RON95 and other bread-and-butter issues throughout the congress.
Taking full responsibility for weaknesses in the party and government's communications, Fahmi apologised to delegates and the party leadership for the shortcomings.
He said PKR must ensure that the benefits of the government's economic achievements were ultimately felt by ordinary Malaysians.
Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said the party's information department was changing its communication approach by holding more frequent, small-scale grassroots sessions to explain government policies directly to the public more informally and interactively.

Title: Affin Hwang trims CelcomDigi earnings projection
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Affin Hwang Investment Bank Bhd has trimmed its earnings forecasts for CelcomDigi Bhd after factoring one-off adjustments incurred in the second quarter (Q2) of 2026.
Affin Hwang cut the company's 2026-2028 earnings forecast by 0.1 per cent to 1.0 per cent
The firm said the impact was partly cushioned by lower future losses from CelcomDigi's 33.3 per cent stake in Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB).
Affin Hwang now expects the transfer of the shares to be completed in early fourth quarter 2026 instead of the third quarter.
CelcomDigi's first-half 2026 (6M26) core net profit slipped one per cent year-on-year to RM816 million, while service revenue increased 1.5 per cent to RM5.43 billion.
Affin Hwang described the results as mediocre, although they were broadly within expectations, with 6M26 core net profit accounting for 48 per cent of consensus estimates and 50 per cent of its full-year forecast.
The decline in core earnings was mainly due to RM43 million in one-off settlement costs and stamp duties, as well as higher 5G wholesale costs.
These were partly offset by lower staff and marketing costs and reduced provisions for doubtful debts.
Sequentially, Q2 core net profit fell 4.8 per cent quarter-on-quarter to RM398 million, mainly due to the one-off adjustments.
CelcomDigi declared a Q2 dividend of 3.4 sen per share, unchanged from the first quarter, bringing its 6M26 dividend per share to 6.8 sen, down 9.3 per cent year-on-year.
Meanwhile, its Q2 service revenue grew 1.2 per cent quarter-on-quarter, supported by stronger contributions from the wholesale, fibre and enterprise segments, which more than offset a 0.3 per cent decline in mobile service revenue.
Affin Hwang said the weaker mobile service revenue was largely attributable to a 0.9 per cent decline in prepaid subscribers.
CelcomDigi's postpaid and prepaid average revenue per user remained stable at RM60 and RM28 respectively.
CelcomDigi also achieved RM100 million in operational excellence savings in Q2, bringing its 6M26 savings to RM140 million and putting it on track to achieve its full-year target of RM470 million.
Affin Hwang said CelcomDigi had underperformed the FBM KLCI by 31 per cent over the past year.
At 20 times its 2027 estimated price-to-earnings ratio, CelcomDigi trades below its 10-year average of 24 times and appears attractive, it said.
The firm believes the negative earnings impact from DNB is largely priced in, although weaker-than-expected earnings and unfavourable developments in Malaysia's 5G deployment plan remain key risks.
Affin Hwang maintained its "Buy" call on CelcomDigi with an unchanged discounted cash flow-derived 12-month target price of RM3.40.

Title: PKR must address public fears, concerns ahead of GE16, says Youth chief
Article:
AYER KEROH: Public concerns and fears regarding Pakatan Harapan and PKR leadership must be addressed if the coalition hopes to recover and win the next general election.
PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Munim said the time remaining before the 16th General Election was urgent and should be fully used by PKR leaders and members to fix existing weaknesses.
"The public may be deceived by sentiments, but if we lack knowledge, awareness, and preparation to lead, I worry we will face a much harder path.
"Our duty starting today is to identify those concerns and fears and offer solutions. It must start with all of us here, both leadership and the grassroots," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today.
Also present were PKR leaders, including party president and PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Elaborating further, Kamil said Malaysia's political system is a representative one that requires political leaders to serve on the ground and convince voters in their constituencies.
"That is what will determine and ensure that our president can be retained for a second term. To the delegates, make that shift.
"Historically, PKR creates a surprise every 10 years. We started in 1998. Ten years later, in 2008, we denied Umno and Barisan Nasional their two-thirds majority in Parliament for the first time.
"Ten years after that, in 2018, under the PKR logo, we succeeded in toppling the Umno and BN regime. Ten years later, which may be in 2028, we will be able to create another surprise," he said.
He said the reform agenda demanded patience but required consistency so that when the right time came, the agenda would continue to be implemented.
"Yesterday, the president also made an announcement close to my heart. It is another victory for university students and youths who have tirelessly fought for university and academic freedom for decades," he said.
Anwar
announced
yesterday that the government would repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Act 30), with the proposal set to be tabled to the Cabinet this Wednesday.

Title: Failure to learn lessons of war is why US faces quagmire in Iran
Article:
LETTER:
United States President Donald Trump said after defeating Iran, the US would take over control of the Strait of Hormuz.
This statement made last Friday demonstrates his exasperation with Iran and his inability to seek a graceful exit from the quagmire.
Military theorist Carl Von Clausewitz famously wrote that war is the continuation of politics by other means insisting that military action is only a tool to achieve a rational political goal.
Applying this dictum to the situation in Iran, we can make one inference: US failure to gain traction in Iran results from a fundamental collapse of policy, where shifting political objectives failed to match the military means deployed.
And where Washington misjudged the strength of its enemy and the interests of other stakeholders like defence contractors, big investment banks, energy corporations and insurance conglomerates, among them.
It also failed to capitalise on its vast experience where despite waging wars around the world - over 36 major wars and hundreds of military interventions since 1775 - Washington brushed off what Clausewitz calls friction and the fog of war.
The twin concepts refer to the difficulties of winning a war. The challenges include morale, logistical support, extreme weather and political interference with the military conduct of the war.
While it is normal in any democracy, for politicians to interfere with the decisions of military commanders on the ground, too many cooks spoil the broth. Likewise changing horses in mid-stream is unwise and counterproductive.
US massive air campaigns against Iran at the start of the war was another blunder the US could have avoided. The US should learn from the failure of carpet bombing in Europe during World War 2.
The carpet bombing did not demoralise the Germans, instead it hardened their popular resistance and turned the conflict albeit temporarily into a costly war of attrition for the Allied Forces.
Like Germany in WW2, Iranian defence/war production facilities are well dispersed and hidden in mountains across its rugged geography which cannot be easily taken out by surface bombing.
The Iran war is also complicated by the presence of multiple stakeholders (mentioned above) with different strategic narratives.
The crisis is no longer a traditional binary conflict where the outcome can be easily defined -a loser and a winner. Echoing Clausewitz, a British military strategist calls for a new approach in understanding the political nature of military combat.
Captain Emile Simpson (Rtd), a veteran of Afghanistan war, observed in his 2012 book "War from the Ground Up: Twenty-First Century Combat as Politics" how contemporary politics constrains military through competing stakeholders demands via their strategic narratives.
Simpson laments that today's war is no longer a war between two states as in Clausewitz era. The line between combat and politics is blurred by more powerful forces wanting to control the outcome of the war.
The dilution of command authority by diverse interests have resulted in US combat ineffectiveness in Iran.
BA HAMZAH
Former lecturer
National Defence University Malaysia (UPNM)
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DAP calls for stronger economic and institutional reform
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo has urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to step up institutional and economic reforms, three and a half years into the unity government's term.
"There are people out there who ask me, three and a half years on, why hasn't this been implemented yet, this is something we need to think about," he said in his speech at the party's National Congress today.
He was speaking ahead of a closely watched vote at the DAP national congress, where 4,264 delegates will decide by secret ballot whether DAP remains in the Federal Government for the rest of the current parliamentary term or withdraws.
Gobind said he and other DAP leaders had pressed Anwar to move faster on the reform agenda.
"I have seen that recently, leaders from DAP, myself included, have asked that the Prime Minister look seriously at the economic reforms that can help the people," he said.
"We have to look at what can actually be agreed upon among all the parties that we can implement, so that we can ensure there is reform or renewal that we need to carry out," he said, describing a coalition government as one that by nature requires compromise between component parties with different manifestos.
He identified three priorities for the government going forward: economic relief for the public, political stability to attract foreign investment, and institutional reform.
"I have received many complaints saying that many more steps still need to be taken.
"We can see that some of the world's biggest companies have chosen Malaysia as the country where they bring their money," he said.
He credited political stability over the past three and a half years with drawing major global investors to the country, citing the strengthening ringgit as a related sign of progress.
On institutional reform, he pointed to proposals the party had raised while in opposition, including separating the roles of the Attorney General and the Public Prosecutor, a two-term limit for the prime minister, and amendments to laws such as the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act and the Peaceful Assembly Act.
He said the party would continue pressing for parliamentary time to advance these reforms, pointing to a recent special sitting on the Tabung Haji Royal Commission of Inquiry as a model.
He suggested similar special sessions could address economic support for small and medium enterprises, student access to university placements and jobs, and issues such as e-invoicing.
"Certain needs must be addressed, particularly when we look at the aspect of Malaysia's ethnic diversity," he said, touching on concerns raised by the Indian community over its place in national development plans.
The vote follows a string of setbacks for Pakatan Harapan in recent state elections, including Negri Sembilan.
Debate was set to be followed by balloting expected to take about two hours, with the outcome determining whether DAP's five ministers and seven deputy ministers remain in the Cabinet through the rest of the term.
"Let us all sit together and think deeply about what our direction truly is," he said.

Title: Malaysian pilot allegedly smuggled drugs abroad multiple times since 2024
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Airlines pilot arrested with about 25 kilogrammes of drugs in Indonesia last month is believed to have smuggled illicit substances abroad multiple times since 2024.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the finding was based on interrogations conducted by NCID officers in Jakarta.
"He has been involved since 2024, acting as a courier to transport drugs out of the country to several destinations according to his flight schedule. This was not his first time, as he had carried drugs to several countries on multiple occasions," he said when contacted.
Hussein said the pilot also
disclosed details
about several drug syndicates in Malaysia and other countries, including Indonesia.
He said the police would further investigate the identified syndicate members, including money flows linked to the drug sales.
Information on the international syndicate network will also be shared with drug enforcement agencies in the relevant countries.
Investigations also found no indication of insider involvement at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) when the pilot passed through security checks.
"Interrogations revealed no signs pointing to insider involvement at KLIA. This means he acted alone when
passing through checks
, and this matter needs to be carefully examined to determine how the drugs went undetected," he said.
He said the police was satisfied for now that there was no insider involvement in the process.
However, the method used by the pilot to bypass security checks was not disclosed to avoid compromising ongoing investigations.
Hussein said the pilot remained in the custody of the Indonesian National Police and must undergo the legal process in Indonesia.
Commenting on the possibility of the suspect being extradited to Malaysia, he said the matter involved bilateral affairs between both countries and declined to elaborate.
When asked about the total number of shipments, destination countries, and payment received by the pilot since 2024, Hussein said the matter was still under investigation.
Earlier, Hussein said the NCID team met and questioned the pilot in Jakarta in a session originally scheduled for last Wednesday and Thursday, which was extended to Friday with their permission.
He said his team received excellent cooperation throughout the meeting, while the pilot was also cooperative.
The 39-year-old
Malaysian pilot was arrested
at the International Arrivals Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Tangerang, Banten, on July 29 after arriving from Kuala Lumpur on flight MH727.
The arrest was made around 11.30pm local time after Indonesian customs officers flagged the pilot's baggage as suspicious during an X-ray scan, before directing him to an inspection room once the luggage was claimed.
Further checks uncovered 14 packages containing 70,114 ecstasy pills weighing about 25kg inside the luggage, alongside 4g of syabu in his carry-on items, with an estimated total value of RM45 million.
According to Indonesian police, the pilot was promised a payment of RM50,000 to bring the drugs to Jakarta before they were to be collected by another individual at a hotel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Husband recalls wife's final day before fatal floodgate accident
Article:
SABAK BERNAM: A 63-year-old security guard said he was deeply saddened at not being able to meet his wife before her tragic death due to his night-shift work over the past two days.
Basar Maslan lost his wife, Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) staff member Selaton Nuri, 55, after her headscarf became entangled in a roller at a floodgate near a hotel here yesterday afternoon.
Basar, a security guard at the Sabak Bernam District Education Office, said he was sleeping at home when his son-in-law called to inform him of the tragedy.
"My son-in-law asked me to check on my wife. Still half-asleep and with numb legs, I forced myself to drive to the scene.
"Upon arriving, I went up to the gate and saw that my wife was already gone. There was nothing I could do except wait for the police and ambulance to arrive," he said when met outside the Sabak Bernam Tengku Ampuan Jemaah Hospital Forensic Unit last night.
The father of six children, aged between 23 and 36, said his wife was closing the floodgate due to high tide while accompanied by their second child.
"Yesterday morning, when I returned from work, I called and asked where she was. She said she was having a drink with our child, and mentioned plans to go to the market, visit someone, and finally head to the floodgate.
"After that, I tried calling her several times but failed. I did not expect her life to be short and that Allah loved her more," he said.
He said his wife, who had served as a gatekeeper for 21 years, had expressed her intention to perform the haj and was waiting for a call to the Holy Land.
"She was a good, generous person who loved to help others. She could not stand seeing people in difficulty.
"She had planned to organise a bread-making course at her factory in Parit 9, Sungai Besar, and was just waiting to execute it, but her intention went unfulfilled," he said.
The body will be buried at the Kampung Bagan Terap Islamic Cemetery today following an autopsy scheduled for 9am.
Meanwhile, Sabak Bernam district police chief Superintendent Md Yusof Ahmad said investigations showed the incident, reported to the police around 4pm, occurred while the victim was
closing the floodgate
due to high tide.
"The case has been classified as sudden death," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hainan free trade port to deepen cooperation with Malaysian, Asean ports
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hainan is emerging as a key gateway between China and the global economy as it accelerates the development of its free trade port (FTP), with new opportunities spanning supply chains, digital trade, investment, tourism and education.
These developments are explored in Bernama TV's upcoming special documentary, "2026: Towards The Hainan Free Trade Port", which offers an in-depth look at how Hainan is reshaping its economic landscape and strengthening its links with regional and international markets.
The rapid transformation taking place across the 35,000-square-kilometre island includes the expansion of Yangpu Port, one of Hainan's key international gateways, which currently operates three main shipping routes connected to Malaysia, with direct calls at Port Klang and Pasir Gudang.
Hainan Harbor and Shipping Holding Co Ltd deputy general manager of production operation centre, Du Chengcai, said the port intends to further optimise its route network, increase sailing frequency and deepen cooperation with ports in Malaysia and across Asean.
"By elevating transshipment efficiency and service standards, we aim to help build a tighter China-Asean supply chain ecosystem," he said.
The documentary also examines how preferential policies, including a 15 per cent corporate and personal income tax rate for eligible businesses and individuals, are supporting Hainan's push to attract digital enterprises and international investment.
Beyond conventional trade, the documentary explores emerging opportunities in medical and marine tourism, international education and Hainan's longstanding cultural ties with Southeast Asia, particularly Malaysia.
"2026: Towards The Hainan Free Trade Port" will air on Bernama TV on Aug 18 at 8.30 pm.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anthropic IPO valuation hinges on US$190-200bil 2028 revenue forecast
Article:
NEW YORK: As Anthropic prepares for what could be one of the biggest initial public offerings (IPOs) on record, Wall Street is looking further into the future than it commonly does to put a price on the artificial intelligence (AI) company, valuing it based on how much revenue it could generate two years from now.
Anthropic is projecting 2028 revenue of roughly US$190 billion to US$200 billion, according to two people familiar with the company's financials, a figure that has not previously been reported.
The projection dwarfs the US$47 billion revenue "run rate", reflecting the firm's current pace of business, that the company publicised as recently as May, and shows the scale of growth investors are being asked to underwrite.
Bankers and investors are using enterprise value-to-revenue multiples based on forecasts, four sources said.
Using revenue multiples is common for high-growth software companies that have yet to establish a mature profit profile.
But looking two years ahead is less typical, reflecting the speed at which Anthropic's business is expanding and the challenges of setting benchmarks for a company still spending heavily to build out its AI infrastructure, the people said.
The pace of spending on AI investment has been responsible for pullbacks in many of the most popular tech stocks in recent months, including some of the firms viewed as comparable to Anthropic.
There have been precedents among some of the fastest-growing companies that hit the market recently.
Backers of Cerebras Systems cited 2028 revenue expectations in the run-up to the firm's IPO this year, and SpaceX projections extended as far as 2029 before the company went public at a record valuation in June, the people said.
The approach reflects the difficulty of valuing an AI company whose margins are still being pressured by enormous spending on computing power, model training and hiring. Investors are betting that as Anthropic grows, revenue will rise faster than the costs required to support that growth, allowing margins to expand.
Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
SEARCHING FOR COMPS
Cloud infrastructure company Cloudflare, enterprise software company Palantir and Elon Musk's SpaceX are among the public companies being considered as reference points for Anthropic's valuation ahead of the company's analyst day, the people said.
Public-market comparables are a crucial part of the IPO valuation process, giving investors a benchmark for how companies seen as having similar growth profiles and business models are valued.
The peer group can also help determine which revenue or earnings multiples should be applied to a company's financial forecasts.
Palantir is valued at 53 times this year's expected revenue, making it one of Wall Street's priciest stocks. SpaceX and Cloudflare both trade at 41.6 times expected 2026 revenue, LSEG data show.
Each of the companies offers a different lens on Anthropic. Palantir has become a reference point for investors valuing businesses with rapid growth and exposure to AI.
Cloudflare provides a comparison with a high-growth software and infrastructure company, while SpaceX offers an example of a company valued in part on expectations for its future scale rather than its current financial profile.
LOOKING PAST CURRENT EARNINGS
Established companies are typically valued more heavily on earnings, or EBITDA, which gives investors a sense of the economics of the business.
For Anthropic, however, current EBITDA does not fully capture the economics investors expect the company to achieve at scale. Anthropic is spending enormous amounts on GPUs and other computing capacity, model training, inference and hiring.
Those expenses are necessary to support its rapid expansion but could become a smaller percentage of revenue as the business grows.
The company's financial trajectory already shows how quickly that equation is changing. Anthropic's revenue run rate was about US$9 billion at the end of 2025, according to the company, before rising to more than US$47 billion by May.
Anthropic has projected revenue of at least US$10.9 billion for the second quarter of 2026, more than double the previous quarter, on track for its first quarterly operating profit of US$559 million.
The company has said its revenue run rate grew more than 10-fold annually in each of the three years through early 2026.
That growth is a key reason investors are willing to look as far ahead as 2028 when applying a revenue multiple.
The valuation therefore rests on the expectation that Anthropic's current spending is funding a business that will eventually generate much higher revenue and margins.
Training and inference could become more efficient as technology improves, while personnel and other operating costs could become a smaller share of revenue as the company scales.
"Could they (Anthropic) get a US$2 trillion valuation, yeah they could and I just wonder if it would stay there over time," said David Merkel, a principal at investment firm Aleph Investments.
"Does it (AI) really produce so much additional productivity... These are just questions that we have to ask if we were thinking of pricing this, buying this."

Title: 'I'd ride around here to 'fly'': 5 'Supermen' held in DUKE racing crackdown
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "After work, I would ride around here to 'fly'."
That was how a 16-year-old boy described his thrill-seeking routine after he was detained by police for performing the dangerous "Superman" stunt during a crackdown on illegal street racing at the Duta-Ulu Kelang Expressway (DUKE) here.
The boy, who no longer attends school, said he would ride around the area after finishing work at a burger stall.
"I was alone. 'Flying' is just for fun. I was afraid, but I still do it," said the Yamaha Lagenda rider, who does not have a licence.
He was among five motorcyclists aged between 16 and 22 detained during an integrated operation along the highway near the Laman Seri Harmoni 33 condominium complex in Sentul.
City police Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Zamzuri Mohd Isa said two of those detained were 16, while the others were 19, 20 and 22.
"All five were believed to be from Kuala Lumpur heading towards Gombak.
"We saw them performing the 'Superman' stunt for about 2km before we detained them," he said at a press conference here following the crackdown.
Zamzuri said the five were detained under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act for reckless and dangerous driving.
"We will also look into whether they have any priors for similar offences," he said.
Another 16-year-old boy, who is still in Form Four, also admitted to performing the dangerous stunt for fun.
"I just wanted to 'fly' tonight from Gombak. Earlier, I went out with some friends, but they got away.
"I was hanging out at a friend's workshop earlier. I borrowed the motorcycle from a friend," said the teenager, who does not have a licence.
Zamzuri said the operation, which began at midnight, saw 778 motorcycles screened and 495 summonses issued.
It also resulted in the seizure of 41 motorcycles, most of which had been illegally modified, including one whose rear brake had been removed.
He said the area was a known gathering point for motorcycle groups in the city and one of several locations frequently used for illegal street racing, alongside Jalan Tun Razak and Jalan Raja Laut.
"The operation followed complaints from residents about large groups of motorcyclists gathering here at night and causing noise with illegally modified motorcycles," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Who's next after Anwar?' Zaliha urges PKR to prepare future leaders
Article:
AYER KEROH: PKR must begin preparing a new generation of leaders capable of succeeding Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and eventually leading the country, party vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa said today.
Zaliha said the party could not afford to wait until Anwar decided to step down before asking who was ready to take over.
She said that in the early years of PKR's struggle, one of its main objectives was to ensure Anwar became prime minister.
"Today, Anwar Ibrahim is already in Putrajaya.
"Therefore, as a mature party, allow me to raise a question that may be somewhat sensitive. Who's next after Anwar?" she said in her winding-up speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre here.
Zaliha said PKR had advocated limiting a prime minister's tenure to 10 years and, if the party believed the office itself should have limits, it must also think ahead about its future leadership.
"Don't wait until one day the president says it is time for him to step aside, and only then do we start looking for someone ready. By then, we will be too late," she said.
She said PKR should begin identifying potential leaders now, providing them with training, exposure and responsibilities, including talent emerging from its divisions, Wanita and Youth wings, as well as professionals, civil society activists and ordinary members.
Zaliha said the question of who comes after Anwar was not about identifying a single successor but to build a generation of reformist leaders.
She also said leadership development should have begun much earlier.
"I want us to build a generation — a generation of leaders who understand the reform struggle, who are clean, competent and courageous, who understand the economy and the concerns of the people, and most importantly, who are ready to lead Malaysia.
"We should have started 20 or 27 years ago. But never mind. Better late than never," she added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mara suspends staff member over sexual harassment allegations involving eight students
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) has immediately suspended a staff member following allegations of sexual harassment involving at least eight students at a Mara educational institution.
Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the action was taken to facilitate a thorough investigation without interference from the parties involved.
He said the matter came to light after he received direct messages from several students claiming to be victims, prompting him to order Mara management to act immediately.
"I tried hard to persuade them to file a police report, as this involves a criminal matter. I find it curious that these students are more willing to complain directly to me than to the management," he said in a Facebook post.
Asyraf Wajdi said Mara would never compromise on any form of misconduct and assured that no cases would be covered up to protect the institution's reputation.
"Do not be afraid to report any misconduct, especially regarding sexual harassment. Mara will never compromise on such misconduct and will take stern action, including dismissal, against those involved," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fadhlina: PKR must remain strong regardless of who stays or leaves
Article:
AYER KEROH: PKR must build enough strength to remain resilient regardless of shifts in political alliances or who chooses to stay in or leave the Unity Government, its Wanita chief Fadhlina Sidek said today.
"Today, they sit with us. Tomorrow, they will negotiate with others. Today, they say they want to defend the Madani Government.
"Tomorrow, we hear stories of them speaking badly about their own partners," she said in her winding-up speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre here.
Fadhlina, who is also Education Minister, said the party must prepare for the next general election immediately, rather than wait for Parliament to be dissolved or candidates to be named.
Without naming any party or individual, she said such developments should not surprise PKR members, noting that the party had previously endured betrayals, the loss of government and former allies turning into opponents.
Fadhlina said PKR's strength should not depend on those currently sharing the political table with it, but on its grassroots members and machinery.
"We must prepare PKR so that whoever is with us, we remain strong. Whoever leaves us, we remain strong," she said.
Fadhlina said PKR valued sincere partners and respected political cooperation, but must continue developing its organisational strength to safeguard the reform agenda.
She also warned those she suggested were already contemplating taking over Putrajaya, telling them that PKR's work in government was far from finished.
"If there are those who have already started calculating when they can take our place, tell them to be patient. Don't get busy measuring the curtains in Putrajaya yet.
"Our work is not finished. Our struggle is not finished. And we are not finished leading the country," she said.
Fadhlina said PKR had survived periods when it held no federal power and must now use its record in government as it prepares to face voters again, while ensuring the reform agenda remained in Putrajaya.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM12bil-RM14bil infrastructure contracts set for second half awards
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Public infrastructure projects worth an estimated RM12 billion-RM14 billion are expected to be awarded in the second half of 2026, giving construction companies a fresh pipeline of work, according to MBSB Research.
The firm said the projects would provide a fresh pipeline for construction companies, as data centre developments continue to drive private-sector growth.
Its analyst Ming San Soong said the visible pipeline would be led by the Penang LRT Mutiara Line's Civil Main Contract 2 package, Langat 2 Phase 2, Sungai Rasau Phase 2 and the Kerian Water engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) project.
The projects should support order book replenishment towards year-end as the rollout of major infrastructure projects under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) is expected to gain traction.
"The next major milestone is Penang LRT, with a project value of RM4 billion-RM5 billion, targeted for November 2026.
"Meanwhile, Langat 2 Phase 2, estimated at RM3 billion to RM4 billion, has entered the procurement stage following pre-qualification for Packages 1 and 2, while Sungai Rasau Phase 2, worth an estimated RM2 billion to RM3 billion, could provide further water-related packages, " he said in a research note.
Ming added that the the Kerian Water EPCC, with an estimated value of RM4 billion-RM5 billion, has also moved closer to implementation following the signing of a 40-year bulk water supply agreement in July, with Gamuda expected to be a direct beneficiary.
He said the construction sector remained on a healthy growth path despite some moderation, with the sector expanding 6.6 per cent year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, compared with 7.7 per cent in the first quarter.
Growth remained broad-based, led by non-residential buildings and specialised construction activities, including data centre core-and-shell and mechanical, electrical and plumbing fit-out works.
Meanwhile, data centre construction awards reached a record RM9.72 billion in the first eight months of 2026, already exceeding the RM9.26 billion recorded for the whole of 2025.
Ming said the average data centre award size had also increased to RM972 million from RM892 million in 2025, reflecting the growing scale of hyperscale developments.
"We also expect a better pickup in data centre job flows in the second half of 2026, with finalisation of up to six large-scale data centre facilities worth RM1 billion-RM2 billion each, reinforcing data centres as the sector's key private-sector growth engine," he said.
Beyond the immediate pipeline, administrative tailwinds could accelerate the rollout of approved infrastructure projects heading into 2027.
This includes the second phase of the Pan Borneo Highway, estimated at RM15 billion in construction cost and the second phase of the Sarawak-Sabah Link Road worth RM7.4 billion.
MRT3, with an estimated value of RM31 billion, also remains a major medium-term rail catalyst.
Ming said Sabah and Sarawak should remain a key focus, with RM93.9 billion already allocated to six less-developed states under the 13MP for roads, water, electricity and connectivity.
About 70 per cent of the planned 2,800km of new rural roads will also be concentrated in these states.
"Faster execution should favour Gamuda Bhd, IJM Corp Bhd, Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd and WCT Holdings Bhd for larger rail and highway packages, alongside East Malaysia-focused contractors as infrastructure rollout accelerates," he said.
The 2027 Budget is also expected to be an important catalyst for the next wave of infrastructure spending.
Ming said the RM430 billion development expenditure envelope under the 13MP for 2026-2030, equivalent to about RM86 billion annually, provides a benchmark for potential new allocations, with at least 70 per cent of development expenditure expected to prioritise basic development.
He said the government also indicated that new rural roads in Sabah and Sarawak will be considered under the 2027 Budget, potentially creating additional opportunities in roads, water and utilities.
Ming added that construction cost pressures appeared manageable, with Malaysian steel bar prices falling for a second consecutive month to RM2,130 a tonne in July 2026, down 1.3 per cent month-on-month after an 8.6 per cent decline in June.
In contrast, bulk cement prices remained firm at RM410 a tonne in July, unchanged since December 2025 and 7.9 per cent higher year-on-year, supported by demand from data centres, industrial developments and infrastructure projects.
MBSB Research maintained its "Positive" stance on the construction sector, supported by record data centre awards and an improving public infrastructure pipeline.
Its top construction sector picks are Gamuda, with a "Buy" call and RM5.60 target price, Sunway Construction Bhd at RM9.18 and Malayan Cement Bhd at RM10.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain expected in parts of Peninsula, Sarawak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit several areas across Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak until 1pm today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) in a warning issued at 8.35am said the affected areas in the Peninsula include the whole of Perlis and Melaka, as well as Langkawi, Kubang Pasu and Kota Setar in Kedah.
The warning also covers Sepang and Kuala Langat in Selangor; Port Dickson, Seremban, Rembau, Kuala Pilah and Tampin in Negri Sembilan; Tangkak and Muar in Johor; and Kuantan, Pekan and Jerantut in Pahang.
In Sarawak, the affected areas include Mukah, Selangau, Sibu, Sarikei, Meradong, Bintulu, Kapit, Bukit Mabong and Subis in Miri.
MetMalaysia said the advisory is a short-term warning issued when there are signs of thunderstorms with rain intensity exceeding 20mm per hour that are close to or expected to last for more than an hour, with a validity period not exceeding six hours.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Civil service integrity showing positive trend, says Chief Secretary
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Integrity among civil servants is showing a positive trend following various government initiatives to strengthen ethical values and empower the public service.
Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said initiatives such as the Integrity and Governance Award (AIGA) had produced encouraging results.
"We introduced these initiatives to strengthen integrity among civil servants. Alhamdulillah, there are signs that our efforts are beginning to bear fruit," he said after officiating the Integrity Fun Walk 2026 here today.
Shamsul Azri, who is also the Malaysian Institute of Integrity (IIM) chairman, said the event served to raise public awareness about the importance of integrity and encourage people to uphold the value in their daily lives.
The three-kilometre and five-kilometre walk attracted about 2,000 participants, including civil servants, government agency representatives and members of non-governmental organisations.
"The most important aspect of this programme is instilling in the public and civil servants alike the understanding that integrity means doing the right thing even when no one is watching," he said.s
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Community, private sector support vital for former Nada clients
Article:
SEPANG: Continued support from the community and private sector is crucial in helping former National Anti-Drug Agency (Nada) clients rebuild their lives after rehabilitation and reduce the risk of relapse.
Nada director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said the lack of post-rehabilitation support, including difficulties securing jobs and social stigma, could undermine their confidence and hinder reintegration into society.
He said vocational training at the Narcotics Addiction Rehabilitation Centre (Puspen), coupled with support after release, could help clients rebuild their confidence and regain their footing.
"When they have a job and are supported not only by employers but also their families and society, the stigma against them lessens.
"Without that stigma, they have the confidence to move forward," he told Bernama and RTM after attending the 2026 New Life Inspiration Programme here yesterday.
The programme, organised jointly by Nada and Boustead Holdings Bhd, involved 90 residents of Sepang Puspen.
Ruslin urged more organisations to give recovering drug users a second chance, stressing that rehabilitation was not solely the responsibility of Nada or the Home Ministry.
"Clients in Puspen will eventually leave. If we do not support them before they leave, they may lose their way.
"Exposing them to the outside world, especially through private-sector initiatives such as sports and motivational programmes, gives them renewed hope upon release," he said.
Meanwhile, Boustead group managing director Datuk Dr Ahmad Sabirin Arshad said upskilling Nada clients would help ensure their potential as part of the workforce was not wasted.
"For us at Boustead and Royale Chulan, the greater impact is ensuring that this human resource is fully integrated," he said.
He said the government incurred high costs each year to rehabilitate clients, adding that helping them return to society as skilled workers would benefit the country.
"The government incurs large costs every year to rehabilitate clients. If we can employ them as skilled workers, the country's aspiration to become a developed nation can be achieved," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi: PKR will improve communications, not control the media
Article:
AYER KEROH: PKR will improve its communication strategy but will not resort to controlling the media, says party information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said the party acknowledged concerns raised during the 2026 PKR National Congress and would make adjustments to improve how information is communicated to the public.
"We are not in the mode to control the media," he said in his winding-up speech at the Melaka International Trade Centre here today.
He said where inaccurate information emerged, the approach would instead be to engage media organisations in an orderly and respectful manner.
"If there is any information that is inaccurate, then we will engage with them in an orderly and respectful manner to inform them that some corrections need to be made," he said.
Fahmi also distinguished the current approach and practices from those of the past, saying that members of the media themselves had noticed the difference.
"In the past... they would be instructed. But we don't do that now," he said.
His remarks came after delegates at the congress raised concerns over PKR's communication machinery and its ability to translate the government's achievements into messages that resonated with ordinary Malaysians.
Fahmi said the party would instead sharpen its focus on issues directly affecting households, describing the distinction as one between macroeconomics and microeconomics.
He said headline indicators such as gross domestic product growth, employment, trade, government revenue and investment represented the broader economic picture. At the same time, voters were more immediately concerned about wages, the cost of living, fuel prices and other daily pressures.
Fahmi said PKR division chiefs had also expressed a desire to play a larger role as the party's "eyes and ears" on the ground and in relaying public concerns to the leadership.
He said the party would continue adjusting its communication strategy to ensure government policies and achievements were better understood.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teacher arrested over alleged sexual assault of Form Four student
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A teacher has been arrested to assist in investigations into an alleged sexual assault involving a Form Four student at a secondary school in the district.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said police received a report from the student on Aug 12 at 4.04pm.
He said the student stated in the report that a male teacher had sexually assaulted the student at the school on Aug 10 at 10.15am.
"The victim also stated that the teacher had previously committed physical sexual assault against them several times.
"On Aug 13 at 11.10am, police arrested the suspect, who teaches at the school attended by the victim," he said.
Azli said a six-day remand order against the suspect from Aug 14 to 19 was granted by the Kuala Terengganu magistrate's court.
He added that an investigation paper has been opened under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which carries a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
He said police are completing the investigation paper, which will be referred to the deputy public prosecutor for further instructions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar launches Temu Fikrah, PKR Youth’s manifesto‑meets‑manual for courage, creativity and Madani governance
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Prime Minister and Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today launched
Temu Fikrah
, a publication produced by the PKR Youth wing (AMK) in conjunction with the PKR National Congress 2026.
The 113-page publication, authored by AMK chief Muhammad Kamil Ahmad Munim and AMK executive committee member Ashraf Ahmad Hadi, outlines the movement’s new thinking on addressing contemporary challenges.
In the foreword, Anwar described the publication as timely, coinciding with the adoption of the Malaysia Madani concept as the intellectual framework and strategic direction for the nation’s administration.
He stressed that the initiative was neither mere technocratic rhetoric nor a seasonal political slogan, but a form of civilisational renewal aimed at re-humanising national development.
“Madani strikes a balance between physical progress and spiritual purity, while anchoring the principles of justice, compassion, sustainability and respect in the country’s governance,” he said.
Anwar also reminded youths, particularly AMK members, that the power entrusted to them today represents a heavy responsibility and a test of piety and moral integrity, rather than an opportunity for complacency or celebration of superficial achievements.
He said rebuilding a nation scarred by past injustices and leakages required extraordinary creativity, intellectual courage and spiritual resilience from the young generation.
Meanwhile, Anwar welcomed
Temu Fikrah
as a manifestation of intellectual enlightenment, expressing hope that it would not merely be read, but internalised and translated into tangible service to the people at the grassroots level.
He said the publication serves as an AMK cadre-building resource, encouraging members to appreciate the history of the struggle, understand the party’s foundations and ideals, and internalise the meaning of “Reformasi”.
Beginning with the emergence of the Reformasi movement and the formation of PKR, the publication explores the principles of justice, policy frameworks, youth activism, and the values of compassion and humanity.
It is also intended to serve as a guide in shaping knowledgeable and principled members who remain steadfast in upholding the mandate of the party’s struggle. — Bernama

Title: PKR’s 27‑year struggle isn’t about power, Zaliha says it’s about changing how Malaysia is run
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Becoming a government is not the end of the Reformasi struggle but rather a real test to prove the courage and wisdom to implement change, said Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) vice president Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa.
She said the reformasi struggle led by PKR for 27 years should not be seen simply as an effort to take over the country’s administration, but rather aimed at changing the way the country is governed.
“Since when has the cry for reform been just a slogan to get into Putrajaya? If our 27-year struggle is only aimed at changing who sits in the government seat, then our struggle is too small.
“Our main goal is to change the way this country is governed,” she said when delivering her winding up speech at the PKR 2026 National Congress at Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC), here today.
Zaliha said that after PKR became part of the government, the party now shouldered a great responsibility to translate the reform agenda through strengthening institutions and governance, combating corruption and abuse of power, as well as ensuring that justice could be felt by all levels of the people.
She said that apart from that, PKR members also need to be brave enough to reprimand and correct any weaknesses that arise among themselves.
“Implementing reform also requires wisdom. Reform does not mean that everything must be changed overnight. There are priorities that need to be determined...there are changes that can be made immediately, and there are changes that require time, negotiation and preparation so that they truly last,” she said.
Taking a lesson from the story of Khalifah Umar Abdul Aziz as touched upon by PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in his speech at the congress opening yesterday, Zaliha said changes need to be implemented in stages without sacrificing the goals of the struggle.
“Gradually does not mean delaying. Being cautious does not mean we have lost the courage to carry out reforms. What is important is that our direction must be clear. We must know what needs to be corrected and we must continue to move towards it,” she said.
Meanwhile, Zaliha, who is also the Member of Parliament for Sekijang, said PKR needs to streamline party communication so that the government’s achievements can be understood and felt by the people.
She said the government cannot assume that the people will know and understand an achievement just because a policy or programme has been implemented.
“I completely agree. We cannot complain that the people do not understand us if we ourselves fail to explain. “After this congress, I hope we can see a more structured, faster and closer to the language of the people party communication movement,” she said.
She also urged the party to master the narrative on social media and not let the space be dominated by the opposition.
According to Zaliha, victory in terms of numbers and policies does not necessarily guarantee acceptance by the people if the party fails to win their “feelings”, thus not taking lightly the importance of mastering the narrative field. — Bernama

Title: DAP’s destiny on the table as Anthony Loke leaves Unity decision to Putrajaya delegates
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — The DAP Party Conference today is the appropriate forum to decide whether the party should remain in or withdraw from the Unity Government, said DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke.
The Transport Minister said such a major decision should be made collectively by the more than 4,000 delegates attending the conference, rather than solely by the 40 members of the Central Executive Committee (CEC).
“We discussed this in the CEC and decided to leave it to the delegates to determine whether the party should remain in the federal government or not. Therefore, the delegates have to make a collective decision for the party.
“As a party in government, there are certainly some constraints and weaknesses that we have to bear together. Therefore, the leadership is leaving it to the delegates to assess whether we should remain in the government until the end of its term or play the role of a pressure group,” he said.
He said this when delivering his policy speech at the 2026 DAP Party Conference at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here.
Also present were DAP advisers Lim Guan Eng and Tan Kok Wai, national chairman Gobind Singh Deo, national deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming, as well as the party’s entire leadership.
Loke also acknowledged that DAP still faces challenges in securing support from Malay voters, following his defeat in the Chennah seat in the recent 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election.
He said his candidacy in the Malay-majority constituency was not aimed at pursuing a personal victory, but rather at proving that DAP could garner support from voters of various races, including in Malay-majority areas.
“I was unable to retain the Chennah seat. I apologise to the delegates for the defeat. I contested not for a personal victory. I contested despite the difficulties because I wanted to prove that DAP can gain the support of voters of various races and that we can win in Malay-majority areas,” he said.
The DAP conference is being held in Putrajaya for the first time. — Bernama

Title: Loke apologises to DAP delegates for losing Chennah in Negeri Sembilan polls
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke today apologised to party delegates for failing to retain Chennah, a seat he had held for three consecutive terms since 2013, in the recent Negeri Sembilan state election.
Loke said contesting the challenging seat was never about personal achievement, but about demonstrating that DAP could win support from people of various ethnic backgrounds and succeed in a Malay-majority area.
“I felt saddened that as the party secretary-general I was unable to retain the seat in the recent Negeri Sembilan state election and for that I would like to apologise to all the delegates for this defeat.
“However, I acknowledge that this mission was unsuccessful and we did not receive strong support from Malay voters or the Orang Asli community.
“This is a major challenge for DAP, how we can break through this racial barrier so that our political journey can go further,” he said in his policy speech during the party’s national congress at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here.
In the recent Negeri Sembilan state election, Loke lost to MCA’s John Kong Choon, who won the seat with a majority of 688 votes.
Nevertheless, Loke stressed that the party’s recent string of electoral defeats should not prevent it from moving forward, as every election has its winners and losers.
“We have almost 60 years of electoral experience and we suffered many defeats during our early struggles but we must not give up.
“To the delegates and party activists, let this be our motivation and inspiration and as long as we do not give up, DAP’s future can still be embraced by the majority of Malaysians,” he said.
