Today’s congress is expected to see delegates deliberate on the party’s position and future direction within the Unity Government.
The congress comes amid growing debate over slow reforms and electoral setbacks within the party, including whether it should remain part of the administration under Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

Title: Asyraf Wajdi suspends MARA staff after eight students allege sexual harassment misconduct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) has immediately suspended a member of its staff following allegations of sexual harassment involving at least eight students at a MARA educational institution.
MARA chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the action was taken to facilitate a thorough investigation to be conducted without interference from the parties involved.
He said the matter came to light after receiving direct messages from several students claiming to be victims, prompting him to order MARA management to take immediate action.
“I tried hard to persuade them to file a police report, as this involves a criminal matter. I find it curious that these students are more willing to complain directly to me than to the management,” he said in a Facebook post.
Asyraf Wajdi said MARA would never compromise on any form of misconduct and gave an assurance that no cases would be covered up or silenced in an effort to protect the institution’s reputation.
“Do not be afraid to report any misconduct, especially regarding sexual harassment. MARA will never compromise on such misconduct and will take stern action, including dismissal, against those involved,” he said. — Bernama

Title: DAP backs Anwar ‘100 per cent’ on AUKU abolition, Loke says reforms must go further
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP today said it will support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim “100 per cent” in abolishing the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU), but stressed that the same spirit must be extended to other promised reforms.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said education reform should go beyond the abolition of AUKU and focus on ensuring equal access to higher education for all Malaysians, regardless of their racial background.
“AUKU is one component, but what is more important in education reform is to ensure equal opportunities for higher education for all Malaysians, regardless of their racial background.
“No Malaysian should be denied the opportunity to pursue higher education because of their background.
“We need to value every Malaysian’s human capital. Every Malaysian who achieves acceptable results should be given a place in a public university, in a public institution of higher learning. This should be the policy and spirit of the reforms that the Prime Minister is trying to bring,” he said in his policy speech at this year’s DAP congress.
Loke added that the party would also support any “proposal, formula or policy” by Anwar that could help reduce the people’s burden.
“We want to announce that DAP will support all these positive changes. We will give our support, but the most important thing is implementation and the firm decisions that need to be made by the Prime Minister and the Cabinet.
“This is something I hope will send a strong message that whatever decisions are made by the DAP national congress today, what is most important is that we want to see positive changes in our country so that Malaysia becomes a progressive nation,” he said.
Yesterday, Anwar announced that the government would abolish AUKU, one of Pakatan Harapan’s long-standing reform commitments.

Title: Fadhlina tells PKR members not to wait for Parliament dissolution to prepare for polls
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Wanita chief Fadhlina Sidek has urged party members to remain election-ready at all times and not wait for Parliament to be dissolved before making preparations.
She said the country’s political landscape was highly dynamic and could change at any time, including the possibility that parties currently in government would choose to negotiate with other political forces.
Fadhlina, who is the Education Minister, said PKR members must be prepared from now and not wait for Parliament to be dissolved or candidates to be announced, as they were politicians who knew what was happening around them.
“We must strengthen PKR so that whoever is with us, we remain strong. Whoever leaves us, we remain strong. We have the spirit.
“We have members who believe in the struggle, who are willing to knock on one door, then another, and then go down another street because they believe this country can change,” Fadhlina said in her winding-up speech at the PKR National Congress 2026 here today.
On the role of women in the party, Fadhlina said PKR must not merely rely on women as campaign workers, but instead provide them with greater opportunities to take on leadership roles.
“Involve them in decision-making, because if we want to convince society, particularly women, to vote for PKR, they too need to believe and see that the party truly believes in women’s leadership,” she said.
On governance, she said the party and government leadership must remain open to criticism, particularly when weaknesses were identified in decisions that had been made.
Fadhlina said the mandate given by the people must be used to do what was right, rather than merely pursuing popularity or taking the easy way out.
“I am not saying that all our decisions are always right. I am also not saying that we cannot be criticised.
“By all means, criticise us; there is no problem, this is our family. If something is not good enough, we improve it,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Control the media? We even give them massage chairs, Fahmi tells PKR congress
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today suggested that PKR will not resort to punitive measures against members of the press, even as some in the party believe its rivals are winning the messaging battle by fighting dirty.
Members of the Pakatan Harapan (PH) anchor party are gathered at this year’s national congress still reeling from the defeat in the Negeri Sembilan state election, which coalition leaders blamed on the opposition’s identity-driven campaign, after PH was ousted following two terms in government.
Speaking to party delegates, Fahmi suggested that PKR had lost the communications war, leading voters to “vote over emotions instead of performance”.
Still, he said the coalition would not turn to harsher tactics to win the perception battle.
Fahmi said instead that his party was treating the press much better than previous governments, joking that it even provided massage chairs to reporters covering the party’s congress.
“Some in the party had asked me why not rein in the media (that help platform rivals’ messaging). Dear friends and comrades, let’s remind ourselves that we are born from the streets, from fighting the power that told the press to attack our president,” the PKR leader said.
“I was told by our friends in the press that it was worse before. They were even told what to write... but today we are so courteous when dealing with them... we even give them massage chairs. You can visit the media room to have a look yourself,” he added.
PH suffered a heavy defeat in the Negeri Sembilan state election after Barisan Nasional (BN) turned to Perikatan Nasional (PN) and succeeded in consolidating a large portion of the Malay vote.
Analysts said the shift in voter dynamics, including among Indian voters and lower turnout among Chinese voters, made it even tougher for the PKR-DAP-Amanah coalition.
The bloc won just 11 of the 36 state assembly seats, giving the BN-PN alliance a two-thirds majority. Two of PH’s heavyweights, former menteri besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun and senior minister Anthony Loke, were also among those defeated.
Fahmi appeared to have shouldered some of the blame for the party’s poor showing. He apologised on behalf of PKR’s central communications team and vowed to improve its strategy, particularly its messaging about the Anwar government’s economic performance.
The minister argued that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s administration had performed well economically, but there was a disconnect between the data and tangible results.
“The comms team would like to say it’s sorry and we will strive to change our strategy, so that the people would understand better what the (PH-led) government is doing and had done, hoping that if they can feel it in the stomach, then it may also nourish the heart,” he said.

Title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain, strong winds in Perlis, Melaka, Sarawak, other areas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit several areas in the Peninsula and Sarawak until 1pm today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) through an alert at 8.35 am informed that the affected areas in the Peninsula include the entire states of Perlis and Melaka, as well as Langkawi, Kubang Pasu and Kota Setar in Kedah.
The weather warning also involves Kuantan, Pekan and Jerantut in Pahang; Sepang and Kuala Langat in Selangor; Port Dickson, Seremban, Rembau, Kuala Pilah and Tampin in Negeri Sembilan; and Tangkak and Muar in Johor.
For Sarawak, the same forecast was issued for the areas of Mukah, Selangau, Sibu, Sarikei, Maradong, Bintulu, Kapit, Bukit Mabong and Subis in Miri.
The warning is a short-term warning valid for a period not exceeding six hours for each advisory. — Bernama

Title: Rafizi: Bersama names 15 candidates early to give Melaka voters time to assess
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) has announced candidates for 15 of the 28 seats in the Melaka state legislative assembly, becoming the first party to unveil its candidates ahead of the state election,
The Star
reported.
The party’s line-up includes Dr Muhamad Solehin Saleh, 40, the elder brother of Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, who will contest Bemban.
Bersama co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli said the early announcement was made before the state assembly is dissolved, allowing voters more time to assess the candidates and their plans.
“We are doing this before Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has even thought about dissolving the state assembly,” he was quoted as saying during the announcement in Melaka Baru last night.
Besides Bemban, Bersama will contest Kuala Linggi, Rembia, Gadek, Machap Jaya, Sungai Udang, Paya Rumput, Klebang, Pengkalan Batu, Ayer Keroh, Bukit Katil, Kesidang, Kota Laksamana, Telok Mas and Serkam.
Rafizi, a former PKR deputy president, said the announcement marked the immediate start of the party’s campaign, with its candidates, members and volunteers expected to begin constituency-level work.
“Our campaign begins tonight. Go out and get to work,” he said.
He said announcing the candidates early would give voters sufficient time to assess their backgrounds, capabilities and plans, while allowing them to build relationships with local communities and understand issues affecting their constituencies.
Rafizi said a team was also preparing a manifesto and policy proposals specifically for Melaka voters.
He said Bersama planned to launch its manifesto during its first ceramah on nomination day.

Title: PAS wants Selangor to be launchpad for toppling PH, says Sanusi
Article:
TANJUNG KARANG, Aug 16 — PAS is targeting Selangor as the starting point for defeating Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the state and subsequently at the federal level in the 16th general election, according to a report by
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT).
The report quoted Perikatan Nasional (PN) election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor as saying Selangor was a key target because of its importance as an economic powerhouse.
“If PH falls in Selangor, PH will fall at the federal level,” he was quoted as saying at a Selangor PAS election machinery gathering at the Selangor PAS complex here last night.
Sanusi, who is also Kedah Menteri Besar, urged voters to judge PH based on its record in government rather than its political messaging.
“Compare it with the performance of previous governments. What has PH achieved? They should show us what they have done while in power,” he said.
PH won 32 of Selangor’s 56 state seats in the 2023 state election, while PN won 22 and Barisan Nasional (BN) secured the remaining two.
PH and BN subsequently formed the state government.
FMT also reported that analysts had previously viewed closer cooperation between BN and PN as a potential challenge to PH’s position in Selangor, particularly if it resulted in greater consolidation of Malay votes.
Last month, Selangor PKR Youth deputy chief Shahrul Adnan called on the state PH leadership to reconsider its political cooperation with BN following BN-PN cooperation in the Aug 1 Negeri Sembilan state election.

Title: Student loses RM29,000 after scammers pose as cops, threaten arrest over money laundering
Article:
IPOH, Aug 16  — Police arrested three local men, aged between 32 and 45, in five raids across Kuala Lumpur and Selangor on Thursday for allegedly being involved in an online scam syndicate.
Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspects were arrested at various locations in Petaling Jaya, Kelana Jaya, Ulu Kelang, Damansara and Kuala Lumpur.
He said the arrests followed a police report lodged by a 22-year-old student who lost RM28,999 after being deceived by individuals posing as law enforcement officers and claiming that he was involved in money laundering.
“The victim, a student at a higher education institution, received a call on July 31 from members of the syndicate posing as representatives of a delivery company, who claimed that a parcel containing illicit items had been addressed to him.
“The call was subsequently transferred to an individual posing as a law enforcement officer, who alleged that the victim was also involved in money laundering and intimidated him with threats of arrest and prosecution,” he said in a statement.
Mohd Alwi said the victim, fearing arrest, followed the syndicate’s instructions by transferring RM8,999 to several bank accounts and leaving gold jewellery worth about RM20,000 outside his house, after being promised that the money and jewellery would be returned once the investigation was concluded.
However, the victim realised he had been scammed when the items were not returned and subsequently lodged a police report on Aug 1.
Mohd Alwi said a team from the Commercial Crime Investigation Division of the Kampar District Police Headquarters subsequently gathered intelligence and tracked down members of the syndicate.
During the raids, police seized eight SIM Box units, 11 Starlink units, 509 SIM cards, a laptop, two routers and five mobile phones.
He said the equipment was believed to have been used as call gateways to manage communication traffic for online scam syndicates suspected of operating from abroad.
“All those arrested were remanded for four days until Monday to assist in the investigation under Section 420 of the Penal Code,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Sultan Nazrin graces Perak Merdeka Month programme with 214,095 student entries
Article:
IPOH, Aug 16 — The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, today graced a programme to instil the spirit of loyalty to the Ruler and country in conjunction with the Perak-level 2026 Merdeka Month at Bangunan Perak Darul Ridzuan here last night.
Also in attendance were the Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, accompanied by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh.
Perak Education Department director Zulkafli Mohamed Mokhtar, in his royal address, said this year’s programme recorded an encouraging turnout, with 214,095 entries involving 83.6 per cent of primary and secondary school students in Perak.
He said this showed that the programme has not only received an overwhelming response but has also continued to grow as an important platform for discovering talent, building self-confidence and developing students’ potential in various fields contested.
“The 15 per cent increase in participation compared with the previous year also proves that the programme is gaining popularity and continues to be a significant platform.
“This programme certainly has a significant impact, not only physically but also on the thinking, values and future of the younger generation, in line with the Malaysia Education Plan 2026-2035,” he said.
He said the initiative is in line with the aspiration of nurturing a generation that excels not only academically but is also morally upright, thinks critically, is patriotic, appreciates the country’s history and heritage, and is capable of becoming credible leaders in the future.
At the event, Sultan Nazrin presented the special award for Best Achievement by District Education Office to the Kinta Utara District Education Office, which received RM20,000 in cash.
His Royal Highness also presented the prize for the champion of the upper secondary Malay Language Public Speaking Competition to Ifwat Arrafi Mohd Amin of Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Tun Abd Razak, Bagan Datuk, while E Johnnes Abysia from SMK Sungai Pari, Kinta Utara, won the English public speaking competition.
Sultan Nazrin also presented prizes for the choral speaking, choral recitation, choir and caricature drawing competitions for primary, lower secondary and upper secondary school categories, while Tuanku Zara presented prizes for the essay writing, poetry composition and poster drawing competitions for the same categories.
Their Royal Highnesses later toured the drawing and caricature exhibition before leaving the event. — Bernama

Title: ESSCom chief: Claims of armed men entering Semporna, Lahad Datu baseless
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Claims of a group of armed men entering Semporna and Lahad Datu, Sabah that went viral on social media are fake, Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCom) commander Datuk Victor Sanjos said.
He also reassured that security in both areas was under control and the public need not be concerned about the claims.
“The viral claims are fake and we are aware of the photos uploaded on social media.
“Currently, the situation is under control and we are continuously monitoring to detect any threat or suspicious activity that can affect the safety of residents and the waters of East Sabah,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
Victor said ESSCom always monitors and implements security control, especially in waters and strategic locations in the East Sabah Security Zone, adding that any information about security threats should be channelled to the authorities for further action and confirmation. — Bernama

Title: Police probe Facebook account owner over alleged seditious, insulting post against royals, govt
Article:
CHUKAI, Aug 15 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) is conducting an investigation into the owner of the Facebook account ‘Ahmad Mu’min’ following a post, which is suspected to contain elements of sedition and insult against the royal institution, the Malaysian government and the PDRM.
Kemaman district police chief Supt Mohd Razi Mohd Rosli said the investigation under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 is being conducted after a report was received from a 29-year-old man at 11.14 am yesterday.
“The police will investigate the identity of the account owner and subsequently conduct an investigation according to legal procedures,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said the latest post from the Facebook account owner, among other things, alleged that the police kicked a motorcyclist during a joint pperation at Pantai Penunjuk, Kijal, near here, at 6.30 pm yesterday.
“The allegation that the police kicked one of the motorcyclists is baseless and this can be seen through the recording that went viral on social media.
“The statement was malicious and the public is urged to verify the content of any post that has the potential to incite hatred against the police,” he said, adding that the operation was carried out following public complaints regarding illegal racing activities that disturb public order. — Bernama

Title: Two drivers detained for allegedly blocking traffic to give way to supercar convoy
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Aug 16 — Police have detained two car drivers believed to have acted as “marshals” by obstructing traffic to give way to a luxury car convoy at Bulatan Lebuh Kota Iskandar here.
Iskandar Puteri deputy police chief Supt Saifullah Jaya @ Yahaya said the two men were arrested yesterday by the district Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division.
He said police began investigations after a video showing the incident went viral on Threads at about 6.16 pm yesterday.
“Acting on a public complaint, the Iskandar Puteri District Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division conducted an operation to trace the individuals involved.
“Investigations found that the supercar convoy was travelling from Puteri Harbour towards Johor Bahru city centre, while the two drivers acted as marshals by stopping vehicles at the location to allow the convoy through,” he said in a statement.
Saifullah said the case was being investigated under Section 110 of the Road Transport Act 1987 for obstruction and interference offences, which carries a fine of up to RM1,000 upon conviction.
Four summonses were also issued for various offences involving non-compliance with vehicle specifications, while the vehicles involved were seized for further action.
He reminded the public that police would not compromise with individuals acting as unauthorised convoy escorts by obstructing traffic or stopping other road users without approval.
“Such actions clearly endanger themselves and other road users,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Ramanan: PTPK financing may be converted from loans to grants
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — The Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma) is seeking feedback and views from other ministries on its proposal to convert Skills Development Fund Corporation (PTPK) financing from loans to grants.
Minister Datuk Seri R Ramanan said the views gathered would be presented to the Cabinet soon for consideration.
“The funds received by PTPK amount to RM100 million, but the condition is that they are provided as loans. Regardless of whether the allocation is used as grants or loans, we need Cabinet approval.
“We have prepared the first paper, but there are improvements and explanations that need to be addressed before the proposal is brought to the Cabinet for consideration,” he told reporters here yesterday.
He said this after a dialogue session held in conjunction with the MYFutureJobs Lindung Kerjaya Carnival, which was also attended by Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) board chairman Datuk Seri Subahan Kamal and group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed.
Ramanan said the initiative was aimed at easing the financial burden faced by students pursuing Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programmes after completing their studies.
Last month, it was reported that Kesuma planned to propose converting PTPK financing into grants instead of the current loan-based system, subject to Cabinet approval.
Earlier at the programme, Ramanan said Kesuma, through Perkeso, had introduced MYFutureJobs Ambassador among higher education institution (IPT) students to increase awareness of career opportunities and MYFutureJobs services within campus communities.
He said the ambassadors would help disseminate information on job opportunities, career development and MYFutureJobs services to their peers in a more direct and effective manner.
Ramanan added that Oyen MYFutureJobs was also introduced as the official MYFutureJobs mascot to strengthen engagement with youths, particularly IPT students, while making the initiative more approachable to the public.
Meanwhile, he said the career carnival by Perkeso reflected the Madani government’s commitment to building a dynamic, inclusive and resilient labour market by ensuring Malaysians not only have access to employment but also receive career development support. — Bernama

Title: Menu Rahmah operators nationwide reach 3,210 as of July, says deputy minister
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — A total of 3,210 food and beverage premises nationwide have registered as Menu Rahmah operators as of July this year, says Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Deputy Minister Datuk Fuziah Salleh.
She said the encouraging response showed that more food operators were willing to work with the government to help ease the people’s cost-of-living burden.
The highest participation, she said, was recorded among food stall or food court operators, with 1,016 registrations, besides restaurants, hawkers, food trucks and bazaars.
“Menu Rahmah is not merely a temporary programme, but part of the government’s ongoing efforts to ensure the people’s cost of living remains a priority,” she said in a statement here last night.
Fuziah said focus was also given to areas with high demand from the public, including Rest and Service Areas (R&R).
She said the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) would continue to strengthen the promotion of Menu Rahmah through the ‘Jom Cari Menu Rahmah’ programme, besides working with more industry players, traders’ associations and food operators to expand the menu options to more locations.
Meanwhile, she said the Madani Rahmah Sales Programme (PJRM) had also been expanded to ensure daily necessities at lower prices could be brought closer to more people.
She said as of July 2026, PJRM had been implemented 19,322 times, exceeding this year’s target of 17,500 implementations, with 25,486,997 transactions recorded nationwide.
“The programme offers savings of between 10 and 30 per cent compared with local market prices and involves various essential items such as chicken, fish, eggs, cooking oil, flour, rice, vegetables, fruits and household necessities,” she said.
Fuziah said PJRM was implemented across 600 state constituencies and 40 zones in the Federal Territories, with a focus on areas that truly need the facility.
Meanwhile, she said the KPDN Mini Carnival at the Melaka level, which began yesterday and ends tomorrow, had brought together various government initiatives, including exhibitions, advisory services, business matching, Menu RAHMAH and PJRM.
She said the programme also offered reasonably priced sales by 27 traders, as well as various stage activities, competitions and an electronic sports (E-Sports) tournament in collaboration with Todak.
“The programme received an encouraging response, with nearly 3,000 visitors recorded yesterday, and the number is expected to continue increasing today and on the final day of the programme tomorrow,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Tengku Zafrul: Reform struggle must deliver tangible results for people
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — The reform struggle must be translated into results that can be seen and felt by the people, said Prime Minister’s Senior Political Advisor Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz.
He said that although various initiatives have been implemented by the Madani government, much more effort is needed to ensure their benefits are enjoyed by all strata of society.
“Good numbers must be followed by spillover effects felt by all citizens. The nation’s economy grew by six percent, outperforming all forecasts, but we must ensure the people reap the benefits,” he said via a Facebook post yesterday.
According to him, the debate sessions at the 2026 PKR National Congress in Melaka today were generally in line with the tone and core message of PKR President Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s policy speech.
The congress, themed “Reviving Reform, Building Madani”, is taking place for two days starting today at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC), Ayer Keroh.
Tengku Zafrul said communication efforts also need to be enhanced so that the people are aware of the various initiatives and achievements of the Madani Government.
“The list of initiatives and achievements of the Madani Government shared by the President earlier is long, but our communication work must also be intensified so that the people know about them. If the people do not know, that is not the people’s fault. That is our own delivery shortcoming,” he said.
He said among the matters mentioned by Anwar were the abolition of the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU), efforts to rehabilitate critical public institutions such as the Federal Land Development Authority (FELDA), as well as several economic initiatives in the upcoming Budget.
According to him, these matters demonstrate that the Madani Government, particularly PKR, recognises that the struggle and efforts for the people are still far from over.
“I am confident that with this approach, coupled with improved working mechanisms and party solidarity -God willing, we will be able to win the people’s trust to continue implementing fresh agendas for the sake of the people,” he said.
He said PKR’s strength depends on the party’s readiness to listen better and strengthen its machinery to ensure the reform struggle delivers tangible results to the people. — Bernama

Title: Penang CM: State remains under control after North Sumatra earthquake tremors
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 16 — The situation in Penang remains under control, with no injuries reported as of early today, following tremors felt across the state after an earthquake struck North Sumatra, Indonesia, yesterday.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government received reports from the Operations Centre of the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) regarding the tremors.
“The Operations Centre received calls from members of the public between 7.23 pm and 7.27 pm (yesterday) reporting tremors at nine locations across all five districts in Penang.
“Following this, JBPM operational teams were deployed to the affected locations to conduct monitoring, involving 36 officers and personnel as well as nine fire engines,” he said in a statement.
Chow said the state government would remain in contact with JBPM and other relevant rescue agencies to monitor the situation and receive further updates.
A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck the North Sumatra region of Indonesia on Saturday evening, hours after a magnitude 7.7 earthquake hit Flores Island in East Nusa Tenggara, killing at least 38 people.
Tremors lasting several minutes were subsequently felt in several areas of Penang and Perak. — Bernama

Title: Northern Sumatra earthquake sends tremors across parts of Peninsular Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — A 6.4 magnitude earthquake hit northern Sumatra, Indonesia, at 6.54 pm yesterday, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said.
MetMalaysia said the earthquake was centred at coordinates 2.9 degrees north and 98.8 degrees east, at a depth of 154 kilometres (km), 37 km southwest of Pematangsiantar.
According to MetMalaysia, tremors were felt along parts of the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia, but there was no tsunami threat to the country.
Meanwhile in Penang, Fire and Rescue Department director Mohamad Shoki Hamzah said the department received nine emergency calls regarding the tremors at around 6.55 pm.
The calls involved four areas in two districts on the island, as well as several areas in Seberang Perai, he added.
“Our personnel have gone to the locations and are conducting further inspections,” he told
Bernama
when contacted.
The tremors, which lasted for several minutes, were reportedly felt in areas including Sungai Baru, Bayan Baru, George Town, Jelutong, Tanjung Bungah, Batu Ferringhi and Air Itam on the island, as well as Perai, Bagan, Teluk Air Tawar, Jalan Baru, Bukit Mertajam, Kepala Batas and Bertam in Seberang Perai.
A Bagan resident, Syahirah Mokhtar, 45, said she was initially startled when she felt the tremors at her home before contacting her child in Pantai Robina, Bagan, who also experienced the same phenomenon.
She said the tremors lasted about two to three minutes, with water in a cup placed on the table visibly moving. She then went downstairs and found that many residents of the apartment had also done the same.
“Many residents initially did not realise that the tremors were caused by an earthquake because they thought they were feeling dizzy. But some noticed that the hanging lights and ceiling fans in their homes were swaying, so we all decided to go downstairs because we were worried that something might happen,” she said.
Also, social media posts indicated that tremors could be felt in Perak, including areas around Kuala Kangsar, Alor Pongsu and Bagan Serai, Teluk Intan, Ulu Kinta, Meru and Ipoh.
“Even Ulu Kinta felt the shaking…,” a social media user posted, while another also reported feeling the same tremors in Kuala Kangsar.
Meanwhile, Perak Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad told Bernama when contacted that the department had yet to receive any emergency calls related to the incident.— Bernama

Title: From rice to remedy: Penang maker’s time‑honoured 40‑day method keeps traditional ‘bedak sejuk’ craft alive
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 16 — Before commercial talcum powders and skincare products became commonplace,
bedak sejuk
was a familiar household staple, used to cool the skin in Malaysia’s hot and humid weather and to soothe the itchiness associated with conditions such as chicken pox.
Made simply from rice and water, the traditional cooling powder was once prepared at home for personal use.
Children and adults alike would often be seen with the white streaks it left on their faces and bodies after being mixed with water and applied to the skin.
Over the years, however,
bedak sejuk
gradually fell out of favour, often regarded as an old-fashioned product used mainly by older generations.
But in recent years, traditional
bedak sejuk
has begun to regain popularity, helped by greater public interest in heritage products, according to maker Yeoh Siong Huat.
The 49-year-old took over Bedak Sejuk Lean Seng from his father in 2016 and now supplies retailers and shops across Penang.
“The method of making
bedak sejuk
has been handed down for generations, but it used to be made at home for personal use until my parents began selling it about 50 years ago,” he said.
Yeoh said his parents had previously operated a small-scale business rearing pigs while also producing
belacan
and
bedak sejuk
for sale.
“When they first started selling
bedak sejuk
, many families were still making their own at home because it was easy to prepare using only rice and water,” he said.
Business gradually improved over the years, and Yeoh stepped in to take over the operation about a decade ago as his parents grew older.
His father died just a year later, leaving Yeoh to continue the craft largely on his own, with occasional help from his brothers on weekends.
Although rice is the only ingredient, making
bedak sejuk
is a slow and labour-intensive process involving several stages.
“The first step is to wash the rice and soak it for a month. Every week, I have to change the water or it will spoil,” he said.
After a month, the rice is washed and rinsed again before being blended into a paste.
The paste is then strained and left to drip dry for between eight and nine hours.
“Once it has dried, I can form the granules. Each batch contains more than 900 granules,” he said.
The granules being dried under the sun. — Picture courtesy of Penang Global Tourism
The granules are arranged in rows on trays and dried under direct sunlight for three days, with at least three hours of sunshine needed each day.
The process is highly dependent on the weather.
“If it is the rainy season, I have to wait for sunny days to dry the granules. If it rains for too many days, the batch may grow mould and I would have to discard it and start all over again,” he said.
Once fully dried, Yeoh uses a fan to remove dust before sieving the granules again to separate out crushed pieces and powder.
The finished granules are then bottled and sent to retailers.
“I have sent my products for laboratory testing to ensure the quality remains good and that they are safe for use on the skin,” he said.
Yeoh packs about 100 bottles a day, but completing a single batch can take at least 40 days, sometimes longer, depending on the weather.
Yeoh packs about 100 bottles a day, but completing a single batch can take at least 40 days. — Picture courtesy of Penang Global Tourism
Traditionally used as part of a skincare routine,
bedak sejuk
continues to be used in much the same way today.
Each bottle retails for RM8, which Yeoh said brings in only enough revenue to cover costs and provide him with a modest living.
“I continue doing this because it is a traditional craft passed down by our ancestors that should be preserved,” he said.
“It is a lot of work and hard labour, and I am definitely not becoming rich from it,” he added.
Yeoh is single so he hoped that his nephews or nieces may one day be interested in taking over the business in future.

Title: Fire dept calls for systematic measures to prevent fallen tree incidents nationwide
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — Incidents of fallen trees in Malaysia can no longer be considered isolated incidents that only occur during the rainy season; instead, they require a preventive approach that is more systematic through regular safety audits, inter-agency data sharing and consistent maintenance.
Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) statistics show that 26,001 cases of fallen trees were recorded nationwide from 2021 to June, last year, resulting in 50 fatalities and 243 injuries.
Its director-general, Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said that emergency calls related to fallen trees remain consistently high, ranging between 4,400 and 5,200 cases per year, while for the first half of 2026 alone, 1,912 cases were recorded.
“During that period, the incident of fallen trees resulted in 50 deaths and 243 injuries, while 360 victims were successfully rescued without injuries.
“This data shows that although the number of cases has not consistently increased, the occurrence of fallen trees still poses a serious risk to public safety,” he told
Bernama.
The media had reported that the Maran Umno Youth chief was among the four who perished in a fallen tree incident on Jalan Lama Bentong heading towards the Janda Baik entrance, Bentong, on Aug 3. On July 19, a 43-year-old man died after the car he was driving was crushed by a fallen tree near the Singapore Embassy on Jalan Tun Razak, Kuala Lumpur.
Nor Hisham said that among the main factors identified as causing tree falls are thunderstorms accompanied by strong winds and heavy rain, especially during the monsoon transition phase.
Continuous rain can cause the soil to become saturated and reduce the stability of the tree’s root system, thereby increasing the risk of the tree falling.
“In addition to weather factors, the physical condition of the trees such as old, diseased, decayed trees or those with weak root and branch structures also contribute to the occurrence,” he said.
A recent investigation by the Penang City Council found that the cause of the 90-year-old angsana tree that fell on Jalan Macalister, Penang, on Aug 3 was due to rotting roots, cavities at the base of the trunk, chronic soil compaction and limited root space.
“JBPM views that tree falls are usually not caused by a single factor, but rather involve a combination of various factors including weather, the physical condition of the tree, and the level of maintenance,” he said,
He said that JBPM supports the implementation of regular tree safety audits and assessments, especially in high-risk areas such as main roads, schools, hospitals, public parks, residential areas, and locations with high foot traffic.
Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said that emergency calls related to fallen trees remain consistently high, ranging between 4,400 and 5,200 cases per year, while for the first half of 2026 alone, 1,912 cases were recorded.— Picture via Facebook
“The audit needs to be conducted by the local authorities (PBTs), the premises owner, or the responsible agency, involving qualified officers or experts. The inspection should include the condition of the trunk, branches, canopy, root system, tilt level, signs of decay, diseases, and the impact of development work around the tree,” he said.
“Trees that have been identified as high-risk need to be acted upon immediately, such as pruning, treatment, support installation, or controlled felling if they pose a threat to public safety.
“JBPM believes that regular audits allow early signs of tree structure failure to be identified before incidents occur, thereby reducing the risk of injury, loss of life, property damage, and disruption to public pathways,” he said.
He said that although the management and maintenance of trees fall under the jurisdiction of the relevant parties, the JBPM is ready to cooperate in terms of sharing incident information, identifying locations where incidents frequently occur, and coordinating preparedness for adverse weather conditions.
In an effort to strengthen prevention, Nor Hisham suggested that the sharing of data on fallen tree incident locations recorded by JBPM be fully utilised by local authorities to identify areas where incidents frequently recur.
“Other collaborations that can be strengthened include mapping high-risk areas, joint inspections, coordinating actions before the monsoon season or periods of bad weather, and faster reporting channels,” he said.
Commenting on operational readiness, Nor Hisham said that JBPM has sufficient personnel, machinery, and equipment to handle fallen tree incidents on a normal and localised scale.
“JBPM also collaborates with local authorities, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Malaysian Civil Defence Force (APM), utility companies, the Public Works Department (JKR), and related agencies to expedite tree removal, traffic control, and ensure the safety of the incident area,” he also said.
He also advised the public to always be alert to weather forecasts and warnings issued by METMalaysia through the official website, the myCuaca app and official social media channels. — Bernama

Title: Sabah teacher uses Jawi to bridge cultural and religious differences in Beluran
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — For Lorenica Frenila Masundim, teaching Jawi script at a school in Sabah’s interior is more than a lesson in writing, it is a way of bringing students and the wider community closer while fostering understanding across racial, religious and cultural differences.
The 36-year-old teacher at Sekolah Kebangsaan Bawang in Beluran sees Jawi lessons as an opportunity to broaden students’ understanding of the national language’s heritage, particularly among those who initially viewed the script as foreign and linked it exclusively to Islam.
Lorenica said she found great fulfilment in seeing non-Muslim students who were once unfamiliar with Jawi gradually learn to read and understand their function as part of the Malay writing system.
“There were students who used to say Jawi was too difficult, but after using the transliteration technique in the application I created, they were able to read it in a short time. As a teacher, seeing their understanding of Jawi change gives me a satisfaction that is hard to describe,” she told
Bernama.
Her Rungus background and Christian faith have never been an obstacle for Lorenica in learning about Jawi, with her role as a Bahasa Melayu teacher encouraging her to understand the script and its place in the national language.
“Just like the Malay language, I have never seen Jawi as belonging to any particular race or religion. To me, it is a national treasure that all Malaysians should learn and preserve,” she said.
Lorenica was first introduced to the Jawi script in 2009 when she took the Basic Introduction to Jawi Writing course for one semester at the Institute of Teacher Education, Gaya Campus in Kota Kinabalu.
Over the next 15 years, she continued to build her knowledge of Jawi before getting the opportunity to teach the script in 2024 and further develop her teaching approach through PhD research under the Ministry of Education’s Hadiah Latihan Persekutuan (HLP) sponsorship.
To help students master Jawi more easily, she developed the PANtaS baCA Jawi (PASCA-ج) application, combining transliteration techniques, interactive exercises and self-directed learning as part of her PhD research.
Lorenica said learning the language or writing systems of other communities not only broadened knowledge but also fostered respect, empathy and mutual appreciation, while helping to overcome prejudice stemming from a lack of understanding.
“Education is a bridge that brings us together despite our differences,  and I believe cross-cultural learning can strengthen national unity, especially through Jawi, which is one of the writing systems used for our national languag,” she said.
Lorenica’s dedication to encouraging wider appreciation of the Jawi script has earned her several accolades, including the Tokoh Ibnu Uraiqith Maulidur Rasul 2024, IMTIYAZ MURABBI Award: Jawi Cross-Cultural Inspiration Teacher 2025 and Sabah Education Excellence Award 2025.
However, she said the Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka Ikon Wibawa Jawi 2024 award held a special place in her heart, coming after a 12-second video showcasing her efforts to teach Jawi went viral on social media.
“I received this award when I was just starting to teach Jawi. At that time, I had not contributed much, apart from a 12-second video that went viral, but I took the award as a trust and responsibility, and it motivated me to keep going and achieve what I have today,” she said.
In conjunction with this year’s National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) celebrations, Lorenica said harmony in a plural society was about being able to live together despite differences in identity, with understanding and mutual respect.
“Sabah is a good example of how communities of different races and religions can live together in mutual respect. As an educator, I believe unity begins in the classroom, where students learn to accept, understand and respect each other’s cultures.
“That is the true spirit of harmony in diversity,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Sabah leaders’ presence at PKR congress reflects strong ties, cooperation, says Mustapha
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor, who is also Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) chairman, and other leaders’ attendance at the 2026 PKR National Congress today reflects the strong ties and spirit of cooperation between Sabah and federal governments.
Sabah PKR Leadership Council chairman Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the cooperation extended beyond politics, encompassing all aspects.
“Our priority is to ensure that stability translates into development, economic opportunities, better basic amenities and solutions to issues that are closely related to the lives of the people of Sabah,” he said in a statement today.
Mustapha, who is also Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs), said the MADANI Government led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had a responsibility to ensure that national development was implemented inclusively and equitably, taking into account the needs and unique characteristics of every region, including Sabah.
He added that PKR would also remain consistent in championing Sabah’s rights and interests, including the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) within a fair federal framework that respected the state’s position and special status.
Mustapha also expressed deep appreciation for the presence of Hajiji and GRS leaders as special guests.
Among the GRS leaders present were Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam, Sabah Rural Development Minister Datuk Rubin Balang and Sabah Youth, Sports Development and Creative Economy Minister Datuk Nizam Abu Bakar Titingan.
Also present were Sabah Education, Science and Technology Minister Datuk James Ratib, GRS deputy secretary-general Datuk Mohd Razali Mohd Razi and Balung assemblyman Syed Ahmad Syed Abas.
“Their presence at the PKR National Congress sends a message that political differences should not be a barrier to us sitting together and building mutual understanding when it comes to the interests of Sabah and its people,” Mustapha said.
Anwar, who is also PKR president, today officiated the 2026 PKR National Congress themed ‘Memugar Reformasi, Membina Madani’ at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here. — Bernama

Title: Auditor-general: Audit reports key to strengthening accountability, transparency and governance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — The National Audit Department (JAN) is carrying out its mandate as the country’s audit institution independently, professionally and with integrity in strengthening accountability, transparency and governance in the public sector, says Auditor General Datuk Seri Wan Suraya Wan Mohd Radzi.
She said audit findings were translated into the Auditor General’s Report (LKAN), which is one of the important instruments in the country’s checks-and-balances mechanism.
She said the Auditor General’s firmness in providing opinions on Financial Statements and making audit recommendations was not merely to fulfil reporting requirements to Parliament, but more importantly, to encourage effective corrective action and improvements in public sector management.
“Through the LKAN, weaknesses and non-compliance can be identified, corrective action can be taken, and systems and governance can be strengthened.
“The ultimate goal is to ensure public funds are managed and spent prudently and transparently, while delivering the appropriate value and benefits to the people,” she said in her speech at the 2026 Auditor General’s Cup Debate Competition (PKAN 2026), themed “120 Years of the National Audit Department: Driving Accountability, Building an Integrity-Driven Madani Generation”.
The inaugural PKAN 2026 brought together 20 public higher education institutions from across the country and was held over three days from Aug 13, with the final round taking place at the Parliament building today.
Meanwhile, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said in his speech that the debate competition provided a platform for the younger generation to appreciate the importance of accountability, governance and public funds management, besides understanding the role of JAN in ensuring that the people’s trust is upheld.
He said the competition was not merely a platform for debating skills, but also an important avenue for developing a younger generation capable of managing differences of opinion in an orderly, rational and respectful manner.
“A mature democracy does not depend solely on the strength of arguments, but also on how differences are respected, debates are conducted responsibly and rules are observed,” he said.
He said Malaysia needed a younger generation that was not only excellent academically, but also critical-minded, courageous in leadership and understood the country’s administrative and democratic processes.
Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) emerged as the PKAN 2026 champions after defeating the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) in the final round, which debated the motion “This House Believes That a Culture of Accountability Should Complement Punitive Action in Addressing Governance Failures”.
UIAM finished as the runners-up, while Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) and Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) shared third place. — Bernama

Title: On-demand car sharing platform, Socar is shutting down in Malaysia after 8 years of operations.
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Users have recently received messages and notification in the app, informing that the service will end on 31st August 2026.
If you have remaining Wallet balance with the platform, you are able to request for a full refund.
Effective today, the Socar app will no longer accept Wallet top-ups and new monthly pass subscriptions. If you have an existing subscription, they will be issuing refunds on a prorated basis.
However, take note that only Socar will cease operations as its peer-to-peer service, Trevo, is still available in Malaysia.
Unlike Socar which essentially works like an on-demand car rental service, Trevo is essentially an “Airbnb” of sorts for car sharing. This is where vehicle owners (the host) can rent out their rides for weekend and holiday trips and earn money for sharing their vehicle.
Socar was officially launched in 2018 and unlike a typical car rental service, Socar deploys a fleet of vehicles across various hotspots including condominium carparks, shopping malls, transportation hubs and hotels, to make it easier for commuters to get a ride when they need to.
The best part is users can rent by the hour and everything is managed from the app including vehicle inspection, unlocking the vehicle and returning the vehicle. It was seen as a potential disruptor to car ownership as it fills a gap to complement eHailing and public transport. With the end of Socar in Malaysia, the next closest alternative is Gocar.
At the time of writing, Socar is still operational in South Korea and they have Koro that’s catered to foreign drivers.
A little over a week before Socar announced the end of its Malaysian car-sharing service, South Korea’s SK Inc, which is the largest shareholder of Socar Mobility Malaysia, was reported to be buying out the entire stake held by its financial investors.
According to Korea Economic Daily, the deal would allow the investors to exit after SocarMobility Malaysia’s planned initial public offering (IPO) did not materialise. The transaction reportedly involves a USD6 million (about RM25 million) debt swap.
SK Inc entered Malaysia’s mobility market in 2017 through a joint venture with South Korea’s Socar and subsequently secured management rights in Socar Mobility Malaysia in 2020. In 2021, private equity firm EastBridge Partners and Sime Darby Berhad invested a combined KRW65 billion in the company, which at the time was valued at around KRW250 billion.
In 2023, SK said Socar Malaysia had 1.9 million members and commanded over 90% of Malaysia’s car-sharing market. —
SoyaCincau

Title: Fahmi: PKR to strengthen communication strategy to better convey govt messages
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) will strengthen its communication strategy, particularly in information dissemination, to ensure the government’s messages are conveyed more clearly to the public.
PKR Information Chief, who is also Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, said the move followed several proposals raised by delegates at the ongoing PKR National Congress 2026 at the Melaka International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITC), Ayer Keroh.
“This is important (to strengthen information dissemination and communication). Many have said that despite various government efforts and achievements, especially those related to macroeconomic matters, these have yet to be translated into improvements felt at the household level.
“This is among the key messages for me, the Communications Ministry, as well as in my capacity as Information Chief and Communications Director of Pakatan Harapan,” he told reporters after visiting the media room during the congress here today.
Fahmi said several views and planned changes related to information dissemination and communication proposals would be presented during the winding-up session tomorrow.
“I remain open to these views and appreciate the willingness of branch leaders who have expressed their commitment to play a greater role in disseminating information.
“Such a channel has existed before, but perhaps a more formal arrangement is needed to ensure issues at the parliamentary level can be brought to our attention in Putrajaya and solutions can be worked out,” he said.
Fahmi said the party’s Central Leadership Council (MPP) was receptive to all proposals raised by delegates and would lead the transformation by making changes within the party’s own leadership first. — Bernama

Title: PKR Selangor delegate calls for party to use own logo in Melaka polls
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — A Selangor PKR delegate today proposed that the party return to using its own logo in future elections, starting with the upcoming Melaka state election.
Ahmad Danish Hairudin, who is also PKR national Youth information chief, said it was timely for the party to campaign under its own logo in the state polls.
He reminded party members that the PKR logo had once represented the Malaysian voice in toppling the arrogance of Umno and the Barisan Nasional (BN) coalition for the first time in the watershed 2018 general election.
“The time has come for Keadilan to use its own logo in the upcoming elections. We start in Melaka, which will face the state election soon,” he said when debating the presidential policy address at the PKR national congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today.
PKR has used its iconic blue-and-white logo in several elections.
Most notably, the party’s logo was used by the newly formed Pakatan Harapan (PH) coalition in the 14th general election (GE14) in 2018, as PH’s red arrowhead logo had not yet been officially registered with the Registrar of Societies (RoS).
That same year, PKR also used its own logo in the Sungai Kandis by-election in Selangor.
In the 2020 Sabah state election, PKR also contested under its own logo, while other PH component parties used the coalition’s logo.
Meanwhile, Ahmad Danish urged PKR not to compromise too much in its political cooperation with Umno to the point of sacrificing the party’s dignity and interests.
He called on the party to instead chart its own political future.
Ahmad Danish cited PKR’s experience in the recent Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections as lessons for the party leadership.
“In Johor, we were back stabbed by Umno. In Negeri Sembilan, we were decapitated by Umno while we were living in the same house.
“So, do we still want to remain silent?” he said.
Ahmad Danish said the grassroots wanted a clear political decision from PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the party leadership on the party’s direction.
He said the leadership should not be too focused on looking after the interests of other parties at the expense of its own members and grassroots.
“Today, the grassroots no longer want the political relationship with Umno-BN, but request that the party’s leadership make a decision to enable the party to move forward,” he said to applause.
The PKR congress comes as the party grapples with the departure of high-profile leaders, resignations of MPs and dismal showings in the recent Negeri Sembilan and Johor state elections.
These developments have also contributed to low morale and growing internal dissent within PKR.

Title: Subang airport runway reopens after helicopter explosion, eight flights diverted
Article:
SUBANG, Aug 15 — The runway at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport here has been reopened after being temporarily closed following a helicopter exploding and catching fire during an engine run-up test earlier this afternoon.
Malaysian Civil Aviation Authority (CAAM) chief executive officer Capt Datuk Norazman Mahmud said the incident occurred at Taxiway Victor, leading to a temporary suspension of flights.
“The runway was reopened for air traffic at 2.57pm. Passengers are advised to check with their respective airlines for the latest updates on their flights,” he said when contacted today.
Norazman said during the runway closure, eight inbound flights were diverted to other airports, while three departing flights had to be delayed.
Meanwhile, flight information displays at the airport showed revised schedules for several flights to various destinations.
Earlier, CAAM had announced that the runway was temporarily closed, with all departures and arrivals suspended until further notice.
The explosion involving a Kamov KaV-32S helicopter owned by a Ukraine-registered company occurred at 12.28pm. The aircraft caught fire during a ground engine run-up test as part of maintenance activities.
Four Ukrainian men comprising the pilot, co-pilot, and two crew members were conducting the maintenance. One of them suffered minor injuries from flying debris. — Bernama
